title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: ADP
providers.scope_notes: Covers ADP Workforce Now / ADP API Central / ADP Marketplace APIs. API Central is a paid add-on for client-built integrations; Marketplace data connectors are partner apps; most ADP developer guides are public PDFs, while developers.adp.com is a JS app and admin/audit docs were not publicly readable.

controls.name: Credential reset (API Central)
controls.what: Reset the project's client credentials at any time.
controls.setting: API Central portal > project > credentials

controls.name: Team Access Management
controls.what: Roles control who can view API credentials and manage certificates; admins can revoke portal access.
controls.setting: API Central portal > Members

controls.name: Project APIs / use case (API discovery tool)
controls.what: A project's credentials reach only the APIs added to that project.
controls.setting: API Central portal > project > add APIs

controls.name: Mutual TLS certificate
controls.what: Every token and API request must present the registered X.509 certificate, so a leaked secret alone is not enough.
controls.setting: API Central / Self Service portal > Certificate

controls.name: Consent Manager - Deny
controls.what: Client admin denies an allowed app so it no longer has access to the organization's ADP data.
controls.setting: https://adpapps.adp.com/consent-manager > Allowed Consents > Deny

controls.name: Consent Manager - Allow/Deny pending request
controls.what: Marketplace apps get no client credentials until the client consents.
controls.setting: Consent Manager > Pending Consents

controls.name: Cancel subscription
controls.what: Cancelling the Marketplace subscription stops the app's API calls for that client.
controls.setting: ADP Marketplace > My Apps > Manage App > cancel subscription

controls.name: Shorter access token lifetime at registration
controls.what: A shorter token expiry can be requested during application registration.
controls.setting: Request to ADP during registration

controls.name: Project users role (API Central Members page)
controls.what: Only members assigned the Project users role can create projects and access API credentials; withholding the role blocks credential creation.
controls.setting: API Central > Members > assign roles

controls.name: Client consent before subscriber credentials are released
controls.what: The partner gets a client's Client ID and Secret only after that client consents to the partner solution.
controls.setting: Consent Manager (client) / Partner credential workflow

controls_unknown: Whether a customer-configurable IP allowlist exists for API Central credentials (docs only say tokens 'may be' tied to an IP).
Whether credential reset or consent denial revokes already-issued access tokens immediately.
What audit/log records exist for credential creation, reset, token issuance and API calls, and how clients access them.
Whether API Central certificates can be revoked by the client before expiry.
Whether consumer-application-subscription-credentials.read returns the same or new secrets after re-consent.

providers.name: Anthropic API
providers.scope_notes: Covers Anthropic Claude API (Claude Console / Claude Platform). Claude Console organizations on platform.claude.com; Claude Enterprise (claude.ai) compliance keys and App Attest device tokens are noted but not catalogued as paths.

controls.name: Maximum expiration policy
controls.what: Console limits key expiration to the policy maximum and removes Never.
controls.setting: Organization policy (UI path not stated)

controls.name: Disable / Re-enable API key
controls.what: Reversibly sets the key to inactive.
controls.setting: Console Settings > API keys, or POST /v1/organizations/api_keys/{api_key_id} status=inactive

controls.name: Delete API key (archive)
controls.what: Permanently archives the key.
controls.setting: Console Settings > API keys, or Update API Key status=archived

controls.name: Workspace-scoped keys
controls.what: A key created for one workspace only works there and cannot reach the Admin API.
controls.setting: Key creation

controls.name: Archive workspace
controls.what: Archives every key created for the workspace within seconds.
controls.setting: Console Settings > Workspaces or Admin API

controls.name: Remove user / archive service account
controls.what: Personal keys stop on user removal; service account keys stop on account archive.
controls.setting: Console or Admin API

controls.name: Member API key creation setting
controls.what: Org setting that allows members to create new API keys (changes logged as api_key_creation_enabled).
controls.setting: Org setting; UI path not stated

controls.name: Archive federation rule / issuer
controls.what: Archived rules reject token exchange.
controls.setting: Console or POST /v1/organizations/federation_rules/{id}/archive (org:admin token)

controls.name: Federation rule token_lifetime_seconds
controls.what: Sets minted token lifetime 60-86400 s.
controls.setting: Federation rule

controls.name: Compliance API (Activity Feed)
controls.what: Must be on for key and federation activity to be recorded.
controls.setting: Claude Console > Settings > Security > Compliance API
controls.plan: Eligible organizations (self-service) or via account team

controls_unknown: Customer IP allowlisting for Claude API requests (not found in docs).
Whether keys or OAuth tokens are subject to SSO / IdP conditional access.
Whether disabling a key or archiving a rule ends already-minted WIF tokens immediately.
Lifetime and admin revocation of ant CLI OAuth tokens.
Console UI path for the maximum expiration policy and the member API key creation setting.
Whether Messages API calls generate Activity Feed events (feed excludes prompt/response text).

providers.name: Atlassian Jira / Confluence Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Product IP allowlisting requires Premium/Enterprise. SAML SSO typically requires Atlassian Guard Standard or an included entitlement.

controls.name: User API tokens (authentication policy)
controls.what: Blocks members in a policy from creating new or using existing user API tokens against the org's apps; takes up to 10 minutes.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > User security > Authentication policies > Edit > Block members from creating a new or using an existing API token
controls.quote: By default, your organization's user API token settings are set to allow access. With the user API token setting, you can allow or block members from: Creating a new API token Using an existing API token

controls.name: User API token expiration (authentication policy)
controls.what: Sets user API tokens of policy members to expire after 1-365 days (or never).
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > User security > Authentication policies > Edit > Never expires / Expires
controls.quote: You can set the token to never expire or set a different expiration date in an authentication policy. You can set the token to expire between 1 to 365 days.

controls.name: API token access for external users
controls.what: Blocks external (unmanaged) users from calling app APIs with user API tokens, including existing tokens.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > User security > External users > API token access for external users > Block
controls.quote: When you block user API token access for external users, they are unable to use a token to access app s through an app API, even if they previously used a token to access them.

controls.name: Revoke user API tokens
controls.what: Org admins can permanently revoke managed accounts' API tokens, singly or in bulk, or via the Delete API token API.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Insights > API token activity > Revoke
controls.quote: You can to revoke one or more of a managed account’s API tokens from one place.

controls.name: IP allowlists
controls.what: Users outside allowed IPs/locations cannot reach Jira/Confluence content, including via the APIs.
controls.setting: admin.atlassian.com > Security > Device security > IP allowlists
controls.plan: Premium (Jira, JSM, Confluence, Compass) or Enterprise (Analytics, Focus)
controls.quote: Users also won't be able to access that app programmatically via the APIs.

controls.name: Block user apps (user-installed apps)
controls.what: Restricts app installation to admins so end users cannot grant third-party (3LO) apps access.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Apps > [site] > Connected apps > settings > Block user apps
controls.quote: Organization and Site admins can also choose to restrict app installation to admin level by selecting Block user apps in the Connected apps settings.

controls.name: Uninstall connected app
controls.what: Uninstalling a 3LO app from the site revokes all users' grants.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Apps > [site] > Connected apps > Manage authorization > Uninstall
controls.quote: For OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps such as “Atlassian for VS Code” , the Uninstall button revokes all users.

controls.name: Marketplace and custom app access control (data security policy)
controls.what: Blocks eligible installed apps from user-generated content, org-wide or in selected spaces; finer allow-lists need Guard.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Security > Data protection > Data security policy > Marketplace and custom app access
controls.plan: Any plan to block all; Atlassian Guard Standard/Premium for selective allow
controls.quote: All organization admins are able to use an override to block all eligible Marketplace and custom apps. The override blocks those apps from accessing user-generated content, such as Confluence pages and Jira work item data in their organization.

controls.name: Service account API token expiration
controls.what: Admin picks a 1-365 day expiry when creating a service account API token (default one year).
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > Create credentials > API token
controls.quote: Select an expiration date for the API token. Token expiration can be between 1 and 365 days.

controls.name: Service account API token scopes
controls.what: Token scopes are chosen at creation and cannot be changed later.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > Create credentials > API token > scopes
controls.quote: Once you create an API token, you can’t modify its scopes. If you want to apply different scopes, you’ll need to create a new token.

controls.name: Revoke service account API token
controls.what: Revoked tokens stop working and are removed, within about 10 minutes.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > credentials > Revoke
controls.quote: When you revoke a token it no longer works and we permanently remove it from your account.

controls.name: Service account OAuth 2.0 credential scopes
controls.what: Admin must select scopes (Jira, Confluence, Goals, Projects only) when creating the client credential.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > Create credentials > OAuth 2.0
controls.quote: OAuth 2.0 credentials for service accounts use scopes by default. The scope for an OAuth 2.0 credential defines the levels of access to data in your Atlassian app s.

controls.name: Revoke service account OAuth 2.0 credential
controls.what: Revoking permanently removes the client credential.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > credentials > Revoke
controls.quote: When you revoke a OAuth 2.0 credential for a service account it no longer works and we permanently remove it from your account.

controls.name: Service account app roles and groups
controls.what: Admins choose which apps/roles and groups a service account has, which bounds what its credentials can reach.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > create/edit > roles, groups
controls.quote: Select roles for the app s that the service account needs to access. You can also add the service account to a group.

controls.name: Delete service account
controls.what: Deleting the account removes all its access and credentials.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > ••• > Delete account
controls.quote: When you delete a service account, this means the service account can no longer access any app s. We also delete the credentials associated with this service account.

controls.name: Create a service account (Organization admin only)
controls.what: Only organization admins can create service accounts and their credentials, so other users cannot mint these credentials.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts
controls.plan: Atlassian Guard Standard or Enterprise (5 service accounts free)

no_control.what: The Marketplace and custom app access control cannot block apps that use Atlassian API tokens.
no_control.quote: Marketplace, custom and other third-party app s that use Atlassian API tokens to access data

no_control.what: Admins cannot create or issue API tokens on a user's behalf (only users create them).
no_control.quote: It’s not possible for anyone else to create an API token on behalf of a user. Users must create API tokens themselves.

controls_unknown: Whether IP allowlists apply to service account credentials calling api.atlassian.com.
Whether OAuth 2.0 service account client secrets expire or can be given an expiry (no official statement found; access tokens last 60 minutes).
Whether the authentication-policy API token block also applies to service accounts.
No per-app allow/block list for 3LO user grants was found in official docs (only the global Block user apps toggle).

providers.name: AWS
providers.scope_notes: Covers Amazon Web Services (IAM, STS, IAM Identity Center, IAM Roles Anywhere, Amazon Bedrock). All features are available in every AWS account; SCPs and centralized root access require AWS Organizations, and Control Tower controls require AWS Control Tower.

controls.name: Deactivate / delete access key (UpdateAccessKey, DeleteAccessKey)
controls.what: Setting a key Inactive or deleting it stops all further use of that key.
controls.setting: IAM console > Users > Security credentials > Actions > Deactivate/Delete; API UpdateAccessKey / DeleteAccessKey

controls.name: Service control policy (SCP)
controls.what: An SCP can deny actions such as iam:CreateAccessKey or iam:CreateServiceSpecificCredential for all IAM users and roles in member accounts.
controls.setting: AWS Organizations > Policies > Service control policies

controls.name: AWS-GR_RESTRICT_ROOT_USER_ACCESS_KEYS
controls.what: Control Tower preventive control (SCP) that denies iam:CreateAccessKey for the root principal.
controls.setting: AWS Control Tower > Controls

controls.name: Root access management (Root credentials management)
controls.what: Lets the management account or delegated admin delete member-account root passwords, access keys and certificates; new accounts get no root credentials.
controls.setting: IAM console > Root access management > Enable

controls.name: aws:SourceIp deny policy
controls.what: Identity policy or SCP that denies any request from outside listed CIDR ranges.
controls.setting: IAM policy / SCP with NotIpAddress aws:SourceIp

controls.name: Time-bound policy (aws:CurrentTime)
controls.what: Inline deny policy that blocks all actions after a set date, giving long-term keys an effective expiry.
controls.setting: IAM > Users > Permissions > Create inline policy

controls.name: Maximum session duration
controls.what: Caps role session length at 1-12 hours (default 1 hour).
controls.setting: IAM > Roles > Edit > Maximum session duration; UpdateRole

controls.name: Revoke active sessions (AWSRevokeOlderSessions)
controls.what: Attaches a deny-all policy for sessions issued before now, invalidating existing temporary credentials for the role.
controls.setting: IAM > Roles > role > Revoke sessions tab

controls.name: aws:TokenIssueTime deny policy
controls.what: Deny policy that blocks temporary credentials issued before a chosen time; does not affect long-term keys.
controls.setting: IAM policy with DateLessThan aws:TokenIssueTime

controls.name: Permission set session duration
controls.what: Sets how long Identity Center role credentials last (1-12 h, default 1 h).
controls.setting: IAM Identity Center > Permission sets > Session duration

controls.name: Deny policy for Identity Center user (SCP with user ID)
controls.what: Pre-staged SCP deny that, once the user ID is added, blocks all actions from the user's active role sessions.
controls.setting: AWS Organizations SCP

controls.name: Import CRL (ImportCrl)
controls.what: Imports a CA revocation list so revoked certificates can no longer create sessions.
controls.setting: API ImportCrl / CLI import-crl

controls.name: iam:ServiceSpecificCredentialAgeDays
controls.what: Policy condition that caps the expiration of new long-term Bedrock keys.
controls.setting: IAM policy on iam:CreateServiceSpecificCredential

controls.name: bedrock:CallWithBearerToken deny
controls.what: Denying this action blocks use of Bedrock API keys; bedrock:bearerTokenType targets SHORT_TERM or LONG_TERM.
controls.setting: IAM policy / SCP

controls.name: Deactivate / Reset / Delete long-term API key
controls.what: Disables, rotates or removes a long-term Bedrock key.
controls.setting: Bedrock console > API keys > Actions; UpdateServiceSpecificCredential / ResetServiceSpecificCredential / DeleteServiceSpecificCredential

controls.name: IAM Access Analyzer unused access
controls.what: Generates findings for IAM user access keys unused within a set window.
controls.setting: IAM Access Analyzer > Create unused access analyzer

controls.name: Role trust policy
controls.what: The trust policy decides which principals can assume a role; removing a principal stops new sessions for it.
controls.setting: IAM console > Roles > Trust relationships / aws iam update-assume-role-policy

controls.name: MFA condition in role trust policy (aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent)
controls.what: A trust policy can require that the caller authenticated with MFA before assuming the role.
controls.setting: Role trust policy Condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent

controls.name: Delete IAM identity provider
controls.what: Deleting the IAM OIDC or SAML identity provider removes the trust used for federated role sessions.
controls.setting: IAM console > Identity providers > Delete

controls.name: Disable user access (IAM Identity Center)
controls.what: Disabling or deleting an Identity Center user blocks new portal sign-in and new IAM role sessions.
controls.setting: IAM Identity Center console > Users

controls.name: DisableTrustAnchor
controls.what: A disabled trust anchor makes temporary credential requests that specify it unauthorized.
controls.setting: POST /trustanchor/{trustAnchorId}/disable

no_control.what: No built-in expiry for IAM user access keys.
IAM policies cannot restrict the root user's permissions.
Sessions of service-linked roles cannot be revoked.
No live OCSP or CRL distribution point checks; revocation needs a manual CRL import.
sts:GetCallerIdentity cannot be denied, so any valid key can confirm its identity.

controls_unknown: Whether long-term Bedrock API keys can be set to never expire, and their maximum lifetime.
Token format/prefix for Bedrock API keys (not documented on fetched pages).
Which CloudTrail field identifies the specific Bedrock API key on a request (key value is not logged).
Default session duration for IAM Roles Anywhere when durationSeconds is omitted.
Exact CloudTrail eventName strings for CreateAccessKey/UpdateAccessKey/DeleteAccessKey were not shown on fetched pages (they match the IAM API action names, which CloudTrail logs).

providers.name: Microsoft Azure
providers.scope_notes: Covers Microsoft Azure (Azure Storage, Azure Resource Manager, Microsoft Entra Workload ID, Azure DevOps Services). Azure Storage and ARM controls are per subscription/account; Conditional Access for workload identities needs Workload Identities Premium; Azure DevOps PAT policies need an Entra-backed organization. Entra delegated/app-only OAuth for Graph and managed identities are covered by the separate microsoft platform.

controls.name: Allow storage account key access (AllowSharedKeyAccess = false)
controls.what: Rejects all requests authorized with account keys, including account and service SAS; user delegation SAS still works.
controls.setting: Storage account > Configuration > Allow storage account key access; ARM property allowSharedKeyAccess

controls.name: Azure Policy: Storage accounts should prevent shared key access
controls.what: Audits or prevents storage accounts that permit Shared Key authorization.
controls.setting: Azure Policy assignment

controls.name: Regenerate key (RegenerateKey)
controls.what: Replaces an account key and revokes SAS signed with that key.
controls.setting: Storage account > Access keys > Rotate key; POST .../regenerateKey

controls.name: Key expiration policy
controls.what: Shows a reminder and enables Azure Policy compliance checks when keys are not rotated in the interval; does not disable keys.
controls.setting: Storage account > Security + networking > Access keys > Set rotation reminder

controls.name: Storage firewall network rules
controls.what: Limits which IPs, VNets and resource instances can reach the account endpoint.
controls.setting: Storage account > Networking

controls.name: SAS expiration policy (Log / Block)
controls.what: Sets a recommended max SAS interval for service and account SAS; Block denies out-of-policy SAS, default Log allows them.
controls.setting: Storage account > Configuration > SAS expiration; -SasExpirationPeriod / -SasExpirationAction

controls.name: Stored access policy
controls.what: Service SAS bound to a stored access policy can be revoked by changing or deleting the policy.
controls.setting: Container/share/queue/table ACL operation

controls.name: Revoke user delegation keys
controls.what: Revokes all user delegation keys for the account, invalidating every user delegation SAS.
controls.setting: az storage account revoke-delegation-keys

controls.name: Conditional Access for workload identities
controls.what: Blocks token requests by single-tenant service principals from outside named locations or when risky.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Conditional Access > Workload identities

controls.name: App management policy (passwordAddition, passwordLifetime, asymmetricKeyLifetime)
controls.what: Blocks new password secrets or caps secret/certificate lifetimes for new or updated apps.
controls.setting: Microsoft Graph tenantAppManagementPolicy / appManagementPolicy

controls.name: Remove credential / disable service principal
controls.what: Deleting the secret, certificate or federated credential stops new token requests; disabling the SP is a CAE revocation event for Microsoft Graph only.
controls.setting: App registrations > Certificates & secrets; Enterprise applications > Properties

controls.name: Azure RBAC role assignment scope
controls.what: Service principal ARM access is limited to its assigned roles and scopes.
controls.setting: az role assignment create --role --scopes

controls.name: Restrict global personal access token creation
controls.what: New PATs must target specific organizations.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Microsoft Entra

controls.name: Restrict full-scoped personal access token creation
controls.what: New PATs must use custom scopes.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Microsoft Entra

controls.name: Enforce maximum personal access token lifespan
controls.what: Caps lifetime of new or renewed PATs in days.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Microsoft Entra

controls.name: Restrict personal access token creation
controls.what: Only allowlisted users (or packaging-only) can create or regenerate PATs; existing PATs keep working.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Policies

controls.name: Automatically revoke leaked personal access tokens
controls.what: PATs found in public GitHub repos are revoked automatically.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Microsoft Entra

controls.name: Enable IP Conditional Access policy validation on non-interactive flows
controls.what: Checks Entra IP-based Conditional Access on PAT REST calls.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Policies

controls.name: Token Admin revoke authorizations
controls.what: Admins revoke users' PATs by authorization ID; disabling a user also revokes their PATs.
controls.setting: POST /_apis/tokenadmin/revocations

controls.name: Block password addition (passwordAddition restriction)
controls.what: Blocks adding new client secrets to applications and service principals; certificates are not blocked by this restriction.
controls.setting: Entra ID > Enterprise apps > Application policies > Block password addition (or tenantAppManagementPolicy via Microsoft Graph)

controls.name: Users can register applications
controls.what: Set to No so only admins and Application Developer role holders can create app registrations (and so add secrets, certificates or federated credentials to new apps).
controls.setting: Entra ID > Users > User settings > Users can register applications

controls.name: Not allowed resource types (Azure Policy) for userAssignedIdentities/federatedIdentityCredentials
controls.what: Blocks creating federated identity credentials on user-assigned managed identities in a subscription or resource group; does not cover app registrations.
controls.setting: Azure Policy > Definitions > Not allowed resource types > Assign

no_control.what: Key expiration policy only reminds; keys never expire.
Azure does not track issued SAS tokens, so there is no inventory or per-token revoke for account SAS.
CAE for workload identities does not cover Azure Resource Manager; ARM tokens survive SP disable until expiry.
App management policies do not affect existing credentials or token issuance for existing apps.
PAT use (token access) is not recorded in the Azure DevOps audit log.

controls_unknown: Whether Azure Activity Log records the service principal identity for ARM read calls made with azure-3/azure-4 tokens (Activity log typically skips reads).
Exact Entra audit activity name for adding/removing a federated identity credential.
Default of the Azure DevOps "IP Conditional Access policy validation on non-interactive flows" policy.
Maximum Azure DevOps PAT lifetime when no tenant policy is set.
Token format or prefix for storage keys, SAS, client secrets or Azure DevOps PATs.
Whether app management policies require a specific license.

providers.name: Bitbucket Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Bitbucket Cloud SaaS; workspace/project access tokens and IP allowlisting need Premium, org-level audit log needs Atlassian Guard; API tokens are Atlassian-account tokens shared with Jira/Confluence.

controls.name: Revoke API token (user)
controls.what: User revokes own token; it stops working immediately.
controls.setting: Atlassian account > Security > API tokens > Revoke

controls.name: Revoke user API tokens (API token activity)
controls.what: Org admin revokes one or many managed users' API tokens.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Insights > API token activity > Revoke; or Delete API token API

controls.name: Require access token expiry
controls.what: Sets the maximum expiry range for all access tokens in the workspace, its projects and repositories.
controls.setting: Workspace settings > Security > Access tokens > Access token expiry date range

controls.name: Revoke access token
controls.what: Admin revokes a repository/project/workspace access token; apps using it lose access.
controls.setting: Repository/Project/Workspace settings > Access tokens > Revoke

controls.name: Access token scopes
controls.what: Scopes and resource container are fixed at creation.
controls.setting: Token creation dialog

controls.name: Delete OAuth consumer
controls.what: Deleting the consumer removes all tokens issued to it.
controls.setting: Workspace settings > OAuth consumers > Delete

controls.name: Restrict access to certain IP addresses
controls.what: Only allowlisted IPs can view private content or clone/push/pull private repos.
controls.setting: Workspace settings > Access controls > Restrict access to certain IP addresses

controls.name: Delete deploy key / SSH key
controls.what: Remove an SSH or deploy key via UI or API.
controls.setting: DELETE /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/deploy-keys/{key_id}; DELETE /users/{selected_user}/ssh-keys/{key_id}

controls.name: Pipelines oidc option
controls.what: Set oidc to false in bitbucket-pipelines.yml to stop issuing the step OIDC token.
controls.setting: bitbucket-pipelines.yml step/global oidc

no_control.what: Org admins cannot block managed users from creating API tokens for Bitbucket.

controls_unknown: Whether the workspace IP allowlist is enforced on REST API calls (docs only mention viewing content and Git clone/push/pull).
Whether API tokens or OAuth tokens are checked against IdP SSO or conditional access at use time.
Whether the workspace audit log records access token creation, rotation or revocation (no such events listed).
Lifetime of the Pipelines OIDC token.
OAuth access token lifetime: developer docs say 1 hour, support docs say 2 hours.
Any admin approval workflow for users authorizing third-party OAuth consumers.

providers.name: Box
providers.scope_notes: Do not substitute Box Shield location/anomaly detection or corporate firewall allowlisting for API source-IP enforcement.

controls.name: Admin authorization of server authentication apps
controls.what: JWT, CCG and Limited Access (App Token) apps cannot be used in the enterprise until an admin authorizes them by Client ID.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > Server Authentication Apps
controls.quote: authorize and enable custom server authentication apps, such as JSON Web Token (JWT) apps, client credential apps, and limited access apps,

controls.name: Re-authorization on scope/access changes
controls.what: Authorization is a snapshot; changed scopes or access level need admin re-authorization.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > … > Reauthorize
controls.quote: The authorization is a snapshot in time. This means that if a developer revisits the Developer Console and changes the configuration, the Admin must re-authorize the application in order for generated Access Tokens to reflect the changes.

controls.name: Disable unpublished platform apps by default
controls.what: Unpublished custom apps (OAuth and server-auth) are disabled until an admin enables them.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Enterprise Settings > Platform Apps
controls.quote: When you select Disable unpublished platform apps by default, Box disables all unpublished platform apps by default.

controls.name: Enable/disable user authentication app
controls.what: Admins enable or disable a custom OAuth 2.0 app for the enterprise by Client ID.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > User Authentication Apps
controls.quote: enable custom user authentication applications, such as OAuth 2.0 apps, and

controls.name: Integration Availability Status
controls.what: Disables a published integration for all or selected users; existing installs stop working.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Integrations
controls.quote: If you disable an application on this page, account holders are unable to add the application to their Box accounts, and cannot use the application if the account holder previously installed it.

controls.name: Enable Integrations by default
controls.what: Toggling off disables all published integrations by default.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Integrations > Settings
controls.quote: Integrations are enabled by default. When you toggle off Enable Integrations by default, Box disables all Integrations.

controls_unknown: No admin setting found that blocks developers from generating developer tokens; tokens expire after 60 minutes and inherit the app's scopes and the user's access.
Whether Box offers API source-IP enforcement for app tokens (no admin doc found; Shield/firewall not counted).
Whether new Limited Access (App Token) apps can still be created.
Whether Box SSO requirements constrain OAuth token issuance for managed users (not checked).
Whether app access level (App only vs App + Enterprise) and scopes can be overridden by the admin at authorization time; docs show them set by the developer in the Developer Console.

providers.name: CircleCI
providers.scope_notes: Covers CircleCI Cloud. CircleCI cloud (Free, Performance, Scale); SAML SSO and audit log streaming need Scale, context security-group restrictions only on github-type orgs; CircleCI Server is out of scope.

controls.name: Personal API token expiry
controls.what: Every web-created token has an expiry of at most one year; DCR tokens last 90 days.
controls.setting: User Settings > Personal API Tokens

controls.name: SSO authentication for personal API tokens
controls.what: Tokens must be SSO-authorized per org to reach SSO-protected org resources.
controls.setting: User Settings > Personal API Tokens > SSO column

controls.name: Delete personal API token
controls.what: User deletes a token from the Remove column.
controls.setting: User Settings > Personal API Tokens

UI label and default for allowApiAccessToAccount; admin-set token lifetime controls not found.

providers.name: Dropbox
providers.scope_notes: Business SSO/app-management entitlement varies by plan. Dropbox Sign is a separate API and is excluded.

controls.name: Default connection permissions: Connecting registered integrations = Block
controls.what: Blocks team members from connecting any registered (App Center) app to their work account.
controls.setting: Admin console > Products > Dropbox > Settings > Integrations > Default connection permissions
controls.plan: Standard, Business, Advanced, Business Plus, Enterprise
controls.quote: Under Default connection permissions , click the dropdown next to Connecting registered integrations .

controls.name: Block specific apps
controls.what: Blocks team members from connecting the selected apps; already-connected members stay connected.
controls.setting: Admin console > Products > Dropbox > Settings > Integrations > app list > Block
controls.plan: Standard, Business, Advanced, Business Plus, Enterprise
controls.quote: You can choose to block your team from connecting to any apps or just block them from connecting to specific apps.

controls.name: Manage custom apps (Not in App Center) - Allow/Block by app key or app ID
controls.what: Allows or blocks a specific non-App Center app (e.g. an internal or unlisted OAuth app) by its app key or app ID.
controls.setting: Admin console > Products > Dropbox > Settings > Integrations > filter Not in App Center > enter app key/ID > Allow or Block
controls.plan: Standard, Business, Advanced, Business Plus, Enterprise
controls.quote: Enter the app key or app ID. If you don't know the app key or app ID, follow the instructions below to find it.

controls.name: Team app installation is admin-only
controls.what: Only team admins can install team-scoped apps; members who try get an error.
controls.setting: Admin console > Integrations (team apps); not a toggle
controls.quote: At this time, only Dropbox Business admins can enable third-party solutions. If any team members attempt to add a team app, they'll receive this error message: ”Only admins can install team apps”.

controls.name: Revoke a member-linked app (team API)
controls.what: Revokes an app that a team member linked to their own account; requires a team-authorized admin app with sessions.modify.
controls.setting: API: POST /2/team/linked_apps/revoke_linked_app (and revoke_linked_app_batch); list with /2/team/linked_apps/list_members_linked_apps
controls.quote: route linked_apps/revoke_linked_app (RevokeLinkedApiAppArg, Void, RevokeLinkedAppError) "Revoke a linked application of the team member." attrs auth = "team" scope = "sessions.modify"

controls.name: Single sign-on (SSO): Required
controls.what: Team members must sign in through the IdP, so new OAuth authorizations require an IdP login; already-linked devices keep working.
controls.setting: Admin console > Settings > Authentication > Single sign-on (SSO) > Required
controls.quote: Required (for production): Team members must log in to Dropbox using SSO, and their Dropbox password will no longer work. Admins can still use their Dropbox admin credentials to log in.

no_control.what: Blocking an app does not revoke existing connections to it.
no_control.quote: Blocking apps doesn’t disconnect team members who are already connected to an app.

no_control.what: Some calendar/contacts integrations cannot be blocked.
no_control.quote: Google Calendar and Outlook Calendar and Contacts are allowed by default and can’t be blocked, even if you choose to block your team from connecting to any apps.

no_control.what: Apps members linked individually cannot be managed from the App permissions page (only via activity log / team API).
no_control.quote: Individually connected apps cannot be managed from the app permissions page. However, you can manage these apps via your team's activity log.

controls_unknown: Default value of "Connecting registered integrations" (allow vs block) is not stated.
Whether switching SSO to Required revokes existing OAuth access/refresh tokens; docs only say linked devices keep working.
No admin control found to restrict OAuth scope or force app-folder-only access, set token lifetime, or IP-restrict API calls.
Exact plan coverage of the team linked-apps API endpoints is not stated in the spec.

providers.name: Elastic Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Covers Elastic Cloud (Elastic Cloud Hosted / Serverless, Elasticsearch). Covers Elastic Cloud org API keys and Elasticsearch-level credentials on ECH, Serverless and self-managed; Elasticsearch audit logging needs a qualifying subscription, and the org-level Cloud audit trail exists only on FedRAMP Moderate.

controls.name: API key expiration (Elastic Cloud)
controls.what: Key expires after a preset or date up to one year, or never.
controls.setting: Organization > API keys > Create API key > Expiration

controls.name: Roles on Cloud API keys
controls.what: Org-level, cloud resource and connected cluster roles limit what the key can do; Cloud-API-only access is default on Serverless.
controls.setting: Create API key > Roles

controls.name: Revoke Cloud API key
controls.what: Deletes the key.
controls.setting: Organization > API keys > trash icon; DELETE /api/v1/users/auth/keys/{api_key_id}

controls.name: xpack.security.authc.api_key.enabled
controls.what: Turns off the built-in API key service for the cluster.
controls.setting: elasticsearch.yml (static)

controls.name: Role descriptors / access on API key
controls.what: Restricts the key to given privileges and indices.
controls.setting: POST /_security/api_key role_descriptors; POST /_security/cross_cluster/api_key access

controls.name: API key expiration (Elasticsearch)
controls.what: Optional expiry; none by default.
controls.setting: Kibana API keys > Create API key; expiration field

controls.name: Invalidate API keys
controls.what: Invalidated keys fail authentication; can target by owner, user or realm.
controls.setting: DELETE /_security/api_key; Kibana API keys > Delete

controls.name: Delete service account tokens
controls.what: Deletes a named service token.
controls.setting: DELETE /_security/service/{namespace}/{service}/credential/token/{name}

controls.name: IP filters (network security policies)
controls.what: Rejects deployment/project traffic from non-allowed IPs with 403.
controls.setting: Organization > Network security > IP filter; apply to deployments

controls.name: Organization owner / manage workload credentials (Cloud role permission)
controls.what: Only organization owners and users who can manage workload credentials can create Cloud API keys; withholding these roles blocks creation.
controls.setting: Organization > Members > role assignment

controls.name: manage_security privilege (cross-cluster API key creation)
controls.what: Creating or updating a cross-cluster API key needs manage_security and an Enterprise license; users without it cannot create one.
controls.setting: Elasticsearch role cluster privileges

no_control.what: Service tokens cannot be given an expiry.
Built-in service accounts cannot be disabled.

controls_unknown: IP restriction for the Elastic Cloud API (api.elastic-cloud.com) used with Cloud API keys.
Whether an org can block creation of Cloud API keys with no expiry (Never).
Org-level audit log of Cloud API key creation/use outside FedRAMP Moderate.
Whether ES API keys owned by a SAML user stop working when the user is removed in the IdP.
Whether xpack.security.authc.api_key.enabled can be set in ECH user settings.
Whether Cloud API key revocation affects in-flight requests.

providers.name: Google Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Covers Google Cloud (IAM, API Keys, Cloud Storage). Covers Google Cloud project/org credentials; org policy constraints and VPC Service Controls need an organization resource; Workspace user OAuth and domain-wide delegation are in the separate `google` platform.

controls.name: iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation (legacy iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation)
controls.what: Blocks creation of new service account keys and SA HMAC keys.
controls.setting: Organization policies > constraint; gcloud resource-manager org-policies enable-enforce

controls.name: iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload
controls.what: Blocks uploading external public keys to service accounts.
controls.setting: Organization policies

controls.name: constraints/iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours
controls.what: Sets an expiry (1h to 2160h) for newly created SA keys.
controls.setting: Organization policies

controls.name: iam.serviceAccountKeyExposureResponse
controls.what: Auto-disables SA keys and SA-bound API keys that Google detects as exposed.
controls.setting: Organization policies (DISABLE_KEY or WAIT_FOR_ABUSE)

controls.name: constraints/iam.allowServiceAccountCredentialLifetimeExtension
controls.what: Lists SAs allowed to mint tokens longer than 1 hour (up to 12 hours).
controls.setting: Organization policies

controls.name: Service Account Token Creator role
controls.what: Only principals granted this role on an SA can mint its short-lived tokens.
controls.setting: IAM policy on the service account

controls.name: Disable service account (serviceAccounts.disable)
controls.what: Immediately disables the SA, which is the documented way to cut off already-issued short-lived tokens.
controls.setting: IAM > Service accounts > Disable; POST .../serviceAccounts/SA_ID:disable

controls.name: Delete / disable service account key
controls.what: Stops the key from minting new tokens; tokens already minted stay valid until expiry.
controls.setting: IAM > Service accounts > Keys; DELETE .../keys/KEY_ID

controls.name: constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders
controls.what: Allow-lists which external IdP issuers can be configured.
controls.setting: Organization policies

controls.name: constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolAwsAccounts
controls.what: Allow-lists which AWS accounts can federate.
controls.setting: Organization policies

controls.name: Attribute conditions
controls.what: CEL condition on the provider limits which external tokens (e.g. which GitHub org) can be exchanged.
controls.setting: Workload identity pool provider > attributeCondition

controls.name: Disable / delete workload identity pool
controls.what: Disabling or deleting the pool stops its identities from accessing Google Cloud.
controls.setting: IAM > Workload Identity Pools > Status toggle / Delete

controls.name: iam.managed.disableServiceAccountApiKeyCreation
controls.what: Blocks binding API keys to service accounts except for allowed services.
controls.setting: Organization policies > Block service account API key bindings

controls.name: API key application and API restrictions
controls.what: Restricts a key to listed external IPs, referrers or apps, and to specific APIs.
controls.setting: APIs & Services > Credentials > key > Application restrictions / API restrictions

controls.name: Delete API key
controls.what: Deletes the key; it can be restored for 30 days.
controls.setting: APIs & Services > Credentials; DeleteKey

controls.name: constraints/storage.restrictAuthTypes
controls.what: Rejects user-account and/or service-account HMAC-signed requests to Cloud Storage.
controls.setting: Organization policies

controls.name: Deactivate / delete HMAC key
controls.what: Set the key INACTIVE or delete it; deleted keys are invalid immediately.
controls.setting: Cloud Storage > Settings > Interoperability; hmacKeys update/delete

controls.name: VPC Service Controls
controls.what: Service perimeters with ingress rules limit API access by network origin and identity, even with stolen credentials.
controls.setting: Security > VPC Service Controls

controls.name: constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders (Deny All)
controls.what: Org policy rule set to Deny All blocks creating new workload identity pool providers; exceptions can allow trusted providers per project. Same constraint as the existing limit_scope entry, used as a block.
controls.setting: Organization policy: constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders

no_control.what: Deleting a key does not revoke access tokens already minted from it.
Issued short-lived tokens cannot be revoked individually; only disabling/deleting the SA cuts them off.
Keys never expire unless the expiry org policy is set.

controls_unknown: Whether existing keys created before iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours was set get an expiry (docs say 'newly created').
Federated (STS) access token lifetime.
Whether API keys support an expiry setting.
Which audit field identifies the API key or HMAC access ID used on a data-plane request.
Whether GetKeyString/lookupKey calls are logged for keys.lookupKey.
Plan/pricing for VPC Service Controls (needs organization).

providers.name: GitHub Enterprise Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Enterprise Cloud feature scope. Fine-grained PATs, classic PATs and GitHub Apps have different approval/revocation rules.

controls.name: Restrict personal access tokens (classic) from accessing your organizations
controls.what: Blocks classic PATs from org-owned resources; public resources stay reachable.
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Settings > Tokens (classic) tab
controls.quote: Restrict access via personal access tokens: Personal access tokens (classic) or fine-grained personal access tokens cannot access resources owned by the organization. SSH keys created by personal access tokens will continue to work.

controls.name: Fine-grained personal access tokens (restrict access)
controls.what: Blocks fine-grained PATs from org-owned resources.
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Settings > Fine-grained tokens tab
controls.quote: By default, both Personal access tokens (classic) and fine-grained personal access tokens are enabled.

controls.name: Restrict access via personal access tokens (enterprise policy)
controls.what: Enterprise owners block classic and/or fine-grained PATs from all enterprise orgs; orgs cannot override.
controls.setting: Enterprise settings > Policies > Personal access tokens
controls.quote: Restrict access via personal access tokens: Personal access tokens cannot access organizations owned by the enterprise. SSH keys created by these personal access tokens will continue to work. Organizations cannot override this setting.

controls.name: Require approval of fine-grained personal access tokens
controls.what: An org owner must approve each fine-grained PAT before it can access org resources (owner-created tokens exempt).
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Settings > Fine-grained tokens; enterprise policy can force on/off
controls.quote: Require administrator approval: An organization owner must approve each fine-grained personal access token that can access the organization. Fine-grained personal access tokens created by organization owners will not need approval. This is the default value.

controls.name: Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens
controls.what: Blocks member PATs whose lifetime exceeds the limit from org resources; tokens are not revoked. Enterprise can set a ceiling.
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Settings (per token type); Enterprise settings > Policies > Personal access tokens
controls.quote: For fine-grained personal access tokens, the default the maximum lifetime policy for organizations is set to expire within 366 days. Personal access tokens (classic) do not have an expiration requirement.

controls.name: Require SAML SSO authentication for all members
controls.what: Members must authenticate via the IdP; classic PATs and SSH keys must be SSO-authorized, and OAuth/GitHub App user authorizations need an active SSO session.
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security > SAML single sign-on; or enterprise-level SAML
controls.quote: You must authorize your personal access token (classic) after creation before the token can access an organization that uses SAML single sign-on (SSO).

controls.name: Revoke SSO authorizations / Delete keys and tokens
controls.what: Owners revoke SSO authorizations (SAML) or delete credentials (EMU only) per user, per credential type, or in bulk.
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security; enterprise incident response; REST API
controls.plan: GitHub Enterprise Cloud (SAML SSO or EMU)
controls.quote: Revoking authorizations removes SSO authorizations for user tokens and SSH keys, either for a specific user, all users, or a specific credential type, across all organizations in your enterprise.

controls.name: Review and revoke fine-grained personal access tokens
controls.what: Org owners view and revoke any fine-grained PAT's access to the org.
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Active tokens; REST API (GitHub Apps only)
controls.quote: Organization owners can view all fine-grained personal access tokens that can access resources owned by the organization. Organization owners can also revoke access by fine-grained personal access tokens.

controls.name: IP allow list
controls.what: Blocks PATs, OAuth app tokens, SSH/deploy keys, GitHub App tokens and GITHUB_TOKEN from non-allowed IPs (not user-installed apps' installation tokens).
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security > IP allow list; Enterprise settings > Authentication security
controls.quote: IP allow lists don't currently restrict access when a GitHub App is installed on a user account and uses server-to-server installation tokens to access an organization or enterprise.

controls.name: Enable IP allow list configuration for installed GitHub Apps
controls.what: Adds IPs declared by installed GitHub Apps to the org allow list so app requests from those IPs are permitted.
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security > IP allow list
controls.quote: If you select Enable IP allow list configuration for installed GitHub Apps in your allow list settings, then IP addresses from installed GitHub Apps are added to your allow list.

controls.name: OAuth app access restrictions
controls.what: Unapproved OAuth apps cannot access private org resources; members must request owner approval.
controls.setting: Org settings > Third-party Access > OAuth app policy
controls.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators cannot authorize OAuth app access to organization resources. Users can request owner approval for OAuth apps they'd like to use

controls.name: Deny access to a previously approved OAuth app
controls.what: Owners remove an approved OAuth app's access to the org.
controls.setting: Org settings > Third-party Access > OAuth app policy
controls.quote: At the organization level, deny the app access. At the user level, revoke the app authorization and its associated tokens.

controls.name: App access requests
controls.what: Controls whether members/outside collaborators may request installation or approval of unapproved apps.
controls.setting: Org settings > Third-party Access
controls.quote: By default, app access requests are enabled. If your organization has a large number of members or outside collaborators, you may want to disable app access requests to reduce the number of requests you have to review.

controls.name: Restrict GitHub App installation to organization owners
controls.what: Repository admins cannot install GitHub Apps or add repos to existing installations; they must request it.
controls.setting: Org settings > Third-party Access
controls.quote: As an organization owner, you can restrict GitHub App installations to only organization owners.

controls.name: GitHub App installation repository access
controls.what: Owners limit an installed app to all or selected repositories.
controls.setting: Org settings > GitHub Apps > Configure > Repository access
controls.quote: Organization owners can change the repository access for an app installed on their organization.

controls.name: Suspend / Uninstall GitHub App
controls.what: Temporarily or permanently blocks an installed app from org resources.
controls.setting: Org settings > GitHub Apps > Configure > Suspend or Uninstall; enterprise owners also
controls.quote: You can also temporarily or permanently prevent a GitHub App from accessing resources owned by your account or organization.

controls.name: Workflow permissions (default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions)
controls.what: Sets the default GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only contents/packages or read/write; workflows can still change it via the permissions key.
controls.setting: Org/Enterprise settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions
controls.quote: Under "Workflow permissions", choose whether you want the GITHUB_TOKEN to have read and write access for all permissions (the permissive setting), or just read access for the contents and packages permissions (the restricted setting).

controls.name: Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests
controls.what: When off, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot create or approve pull requests.
controls.setting: Org/Enterprise settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions
controls.quote: By default, when you create a new organization, workflows are not allowed to create or approve pull requests.

controls.name: Send write tokens to workflows from pull requests (fork PRs)
controls.what: Controls whether fork pull-request workflows get a write GITHUB_TOKEN; otherwise it is read-only.
controls.setting: Org/Enterprise settings > Actions > General > Fork pull request workflows
controls.quote: Run workflows from fork pull requests. Users can run workflows from fork pull requests. By default, workflows will use a GITHUB_TOKEN with read-only permission, with no access to secrets.

controls.name: Actions policies (disable GitHub Actions)
controls.what: Disabling Actions for all or selected repositories prevents workflows (and their GITHUB_TOKEN) from running.
controls.setting: Org settings > Actions > General > Policies; enterprise policy can override
controls.quote: You can choose to disable GitHub Actions for all repositories in your organization, or only allow specific repositories.

controls.name: Deploy keys (allow/disallow creation)
controls.what: Disallowing deploy keys blocks creation and disables existing deploy keys in all org repos.
controls.setting: Org settings > Repository > Deploy keys; Enterprise settings > Policies > Repository > Deploy keys
controls.quote: By default, new organizations are configured to disallow the creation of deploy keys in repositories.

controls.name: Enforcing a policy for deploy keys (enterprise)
controls.what: Enterprise owners allow, restrict, or delegate deploy key creation for all orgs; disabling disables existing keys.
controls.setting: Enterprise settings > Policies > Repository > Deploy keys
controls.quote: Changing this setting to disabled will result in existing deploy keys being disabled in all repositories in the enterprise.

no_control.what: Classic PATs cannot be put under an approval workflow; only fine-grained PATs can.
no_control.quote: Only fine-grained personal access tokens, not personal access tokens (classic), are subject to approval.

no_control.what: Enterprise revoke/delete credential actions do not cover GitHub App installation tokens, deploy keys or GITHUB_TOKEN.
no_control.quote: The following credential types are not affected by either action: GitHub App installation tokens (ghs_) Deploy keys GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN access

no_control.what: Admins cannot stop repo writers from raising GITHUB_TOKEN permissions in the workflow file above the default.
no_control.quote: Anyone with write access to a repository can modify the permissions granted to the GITHUB_TOKEN, adding or removing access as required, by editing the permissions key in the workflow file.

no_control.what: GitHub Apps are not subject to the OAuth app access policy.
no_control.quote: GitHub Apps aren't subject to organization application policies. A GitHub App only has access to the repositories an organization owner has granted.

controls_unknown: Whether admins can set a maximum lifetime for GitHub App user access tokens or OAuth app tokens (only app-developer settings found).
Whether GITHUB_TOKEN workflow permission defaults can be made non-overridable.

providers.name: GitLab.com
providers.scope_notes: Group IP controls require Premium/Ultimate. Do not transfer Self-Managed 400-day/configuration options to GitLab.com.

controls.name: Require fine-grained personal access tokens after a specific date
controls.what: After the date, legacy PATs cannot access the top-level group, subgroups or projects; group/project/service-account tokens are exempt.
controls.setting: Top-level group > Settings > General > Permissions and group features
controls.quote: On GitLab.com, enforcement applies to the group and its subgroups and projects, and blocks legacy personal access tokens from accessing those resources after the enforcement date.

controls.name: Disable personal access tokens (enterprise users)
controls.what: Stops the group's enterprise users from creating PATs and disables their existing PATs; service account PATs unaffected.
controls.setting: Group > Settings > General > Permissions and group features > Enterprise users
controls.quote: Stops the enterprise users from creating new personal access tokens. This behavior applies even if an enterprise user is also an administrator of the group. Disables the existing personal access tokens of the enterprise users.

controls.name: Users can create group access tokens and project access tokens in this group
controls.what: Clearing it blocks new group/project access tokens across the group; existing ones stay valid.
controls.setting: Top-level group > Settings > General > Permissions and group features
controls.quote: The restriction covers the entire group, including all subgroups and their projects. Existing tokens remain valid until they expire or you revoke them.

controls.name: Restrict access by IP address
controls.what: Limits UI and API access to the group to listed CIDRs, including group/project tokens, deploy keys and CI clone operations.
controls.setting: Top-level group > Settings > General > Permissions and group features
controls.quote: IP restrictions apply to project and group access tokens, service accounts, deploy keys, and deploy tokens.

controls.name: Enforce SSO-only authentication for Git and Dependency Proxy activity
controls.what: Git over HTTPS/SSH and Git-related API calls by users need an active SSO session; not enforced for bot tokens or CI jobs.
controls.setting: Group > Settings > SAML SSO
controls.quote: For Git activity over SSH and HTTPS, users must have at least one active session signed-in through SSO before they can push to or pull from a GitLab repository.

controls.name: Credentials inventory (revoke tokens)
controls.what: Top-level group owners view and revoke enterprise users' PATs and group/project access tokens.
controls.setting: Group > Secure > Credentials inventory
controls.quote: On GitLab.com, the credentials inventory monitors enterprise users and service accounts in a top-level group.

controls.name: CI/CD job token allowlist
controls.what: Only jobs from the project itself and allowlisted groups/projects can use a job token against this project.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions
controls.quote: By default, job token access is restricted to only CI/CD jobs that run in pipelines in your project.

controls.name: Fine-grained permissions for job tokens
controls.what: Limits allowlisted job tokens to a set of REST API endpoints.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions (allowlist entry)
controls.quote: You can use fine-grained permissions to explicitly allow access to a limited set of REST API endpoints.

controls.name: Allow Git push requests to the repository
controls.what: Off by default; when off job tokens cannot push to the repository.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions; projects API
controls.quote: You can configure your project to allow Git push requests that are authenticated with a CI/CD job token. This setting is turned off by default.

controls.name: Limit job token scope for public or internal projects (feature visibility)
controls.what: Setting features to 'Only project members' stops non-allowlisted job tokens reading artifacts, registries, releases or the repo.
controls.setting: Project > Settings > General > Visibility, project features, permissions
controls.quote: You can limit access to these actions to only the projects on the allowlist by setting each feature to be only visible to project members.

no_control.what: Group SSO enforcement does not apply to API requests (PAT or OAuth).
no_control.quote: SSO enforcement does not apply to API requests. However, you can disable password and passkey authentication for enterprise users to prevent password-based API access.

no_control.what: Web SSO enforcement does not cover project/group access tokens, service accounts or deploy keys.
no_control.quote: Credentials that are not tied to regular users (for example, project and group access tokens, service accounts, and deploy keys) do not have the SSO check enforced.

no_control.what: Fine-grained token enforcement does not cover service account, group or project access tokens.
no_control.quote: Enforcement does not apply to tokens for service accounts, group access tokens, or project access tokens.

no_control.what: Group IP restrictions do not cover runner registration or job requests.
no_control.quote: IP restrictions do not apply to runner registration or when runners request or update CI/CD jobs.

controls_unknown: Whether a GitLab.com group owner can block or allowlist third-party OAuth applications that members authorize (no group-level control found).
Whether a GitLab.com group owner can set a shorter maximum token lifetime than the 365-day default (docs describe this only for administrators/Self-Managed).

providers.name: Glean
providers.scope_notes: Glean-hosted enterprise SaaS (single tenant, <instance>-be.glean.com); plan tiers are not documented for these controls, and log delivery to customer storage needs Glean account team setup.

controls.name: Revoke API token
controls.what: Revokes a Glean-issued token.
controls.setting: Admin console > Platform > API tokens

controls.name: Token scopes
controls.what: Token is limited to chosen Client API scopes, fixed at creation.
controls.setting: Add New Token > Scopes

controls.name: Agent-scoped Client API token
controls.what: Token only works for the assigned agents and expires after one year.
controls.setting: API tokens page or agent Share > API

controls.name: Token creation roles
controls.what: Only admin roles or API Token Creator can create tokens; global scope needs Super Admin.
controls.setting: Admin console > User roles

controls.name: Greenlisted IPs
controls.what: Per-token CIDR allowlist enforced on Indexing API requests.
controls.setting: Indexing token creation > Greenlisted IPs

controls.name: Expires On (required)
controls.what: Indexing tokens must have an expiry date.
controls.setting: Indexing token creation

controls.name: Rotation Period
controls.what: Token must be rotated via /rotatetoken within the set period (min 24h).
controls.setting: Indexing token creation > Rotation Settings

controls.name: Tenant-wide IP greenlist
controls.what: VPC firewall allowlist for the tenant; MCP also checks at app layer.
controls.setting: Not documented (Glean-managed)

controls.name: Enable Glean OAuth Server
controls.what: Turns Glean-issued OAuth on or off.
controls.setting: Admin console > Settings > Third-party access (OAuth)

controls.name: Dynamic client registration settings
controls.what: Allow any app, only approved apps/redirect URIs, or no DCR.
controls.setting: Settings > Third-party access (OAuth) > DCR > Manage settings

controls.name: Delete static client / Revoke client
controls.what: Ends access for all users of that client after config propagation.
controls.setting: Users & permissions > Third-party access (OAuth) > Delete client

controls.name: Rotate secret (static client)
controls.what: Old client secret stops working immediately.
controls.setting: Edit client > Rotate secret

controls.name: OAuth token TTL
controls.what: Admins can change access (7d) and refresh (180d) TTLs.
controls.setting: Not documented

controls.name: Sign out of all sessions
controls.what: Invalidates a user's Glean-issued OAuth tokens (cache refresh ~10 min).
controls.setting: Admin console (user)

controls.name: Enable IDP OAuth for API access
controls.what: Turns on acceptance of IdP tokens for listed client IDs.
controls.setting: Settings > Third-party access (OAuth)

controls.name: Enterprise Managed Auth (trusted issuer, allowed scopes)
controls.what: EMA tokens limited to selected scopes; rejected without a trusted issuer.
controls.setting: Users & permissions > Third-party access (OAuth) > Enterprise Managed Auth

no_control.what: Token scopes and permission type cannot be edited after creation; must reissue.
OAuth/federated auth is not available for the Indexing API; only static Glean-issued tokens.

controls_unknown: Whether revoking a Glean-issued API token takes effect immediately
Whether user deprovisioning revokes that user's Glean-issued API tokens
Whether admin audit logs record API token create/revoke (coverage list does not mention tokens)
Per-token IP allowlist for Client API tokens
Default OAuth server state (admin docs: off; developer docs: on)
Where the tenant-wide IP greenlist is configured and whether customers manage it
EMA token lifetime

providers.name: Google Workspace
providers.scope_notes: Context-Aware Access requires eligible Workspace/Cloud Identity editions. User policy coverage does not establish protection of DWD service accounts.

controls.name: App access control: Blocked / Limited / Specific Google data / Trusted
controls.what: Per OAuth app, blocks it, limits it to unrestricted services, or limits it to admin-chosen scopes.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Third-Party App Access
controls.quote: Can request data access only to scopes that you specify when configuring the app.

controls.name: Unconfigured third-party apps
controls.what: Blocks Sign in with Google to apps the admin has not configured, or allows only basic-profile requests.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Settings > Unconfigured third-party apps
controls.quote: Users can't sign in with Google to any third-party apps and websites until you configure those apps and sites

controls.name: Allow users to request access to unconfigured third-party apps
controls.what: Users blocked from an unconfigured app can request it; admins review the request.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Settings
controls.quote: check the Allow users to request access to unconfigured third-party apps box.

controls.name: Google services: Restricted
controls.what: Marks a Workspace service so only Trusted or Specific-data apps can reach its data.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Google Services
controls.quote: Only internal and third-party apps configured with a Trusted or Specific Google data access setting can access data.

controls.name: Restrict high-risk OAuth scopes
controls.what: For Gmail, Drive, Docs and Chat, blocks a predefined list of high-risk scopes for non-trusted apps.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Google Services
controls.quote: Gmail, Google Drive, Docs, and Chat can also restrict access to a predefined list of high-risk OAuth scopes.

controls.name: Trust internal apps
controls.what: When checked, all internal apps can reach restricted APIs; leaving it off keeps internal apps under the same restrictions.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Settings
controls.quote: To allow API access for all internal apps, check the Trust internal apps box.

controls.name: Access levels for OAuth apps (Context-Aware Access)
controls.what: Requires IP, location, device or identity conditions when users sign in to OAuth apps with Google; checked at sign-in only.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > Context-Aware Access > General Settings > Access levels for OAuth apps
controls.plan: Frontline, Enterprise, Education, Enterprise Essentials Plus, Cloud Identity Premium
controls.quote: Context-Aware Access rules are applied only when a user signs in through Google.

controls.name: Context-Aware Access for Workspace APIs
controls.what: Applies CAA access levels to first- and third-party apps reaching Workspace core data through APIs.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > Context-Aware Access
controls.plan: Enterprise Standard/Plus, Education Standard/Plus, Cloud Identity Premium
controls.quote: Admins can now use context-aware access to block users' access to Workspace Applications

controls.name: Google Cloud session control
controls.what: Forces reauthentication every 1-24 hours for apps holding user grants to Google Cloud scopes, similar to revoking their refresh tokens.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > Google Cloud session control
controls.quote: analogous to what would happen if an admin revoked the refresh tokens for that application.

controls.name: Manage Domain Wide Delegation
controls.what: Super admins authorize each service account or OAuth client ID with an explicit scope list; editing scopes or deleting the client stops access.
controls.setting: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Domain Wide Delegation
controls.quote: add each scope that the application can access (should be appropriately narrow).

controls.name: Multi-party approval for domain-wide delegation
controls.what: When enabled, adding, editing or deleting a DWD client needs a second super admin's approval.
controls.setting: Admin console multi-party approval settings
controls.quote: requires approval from another super admin.

controls.name: iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation / iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation
controls.what: Org policy that blocks creation of user-managed service account keys used to sign DWD JWTs.
controls.setting: Google Cloud Organization Policy (constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation)
controls.quote: If your organization was created on or after May 3, 2024, this constraint is enforced by default.

controls.name: iam.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload
controls.what: Org policy that blocks uploading external public keys to service accounts.
controls.setting: Google Cloud Organization Policy (constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload)
controls.quote: When this constraint is set, users cannot upload public keys to service accounts in projects affected by the constraint.

controls.name: iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours
controls.what: Org policy that sets a maximum lifetime for new service account keys, which otherwise never expire.
controls.setting: Google Cloud Organization Policy (constraints/iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours)
controls.quote: A service account key lets you authenticate a request as a service account. By default, service account keys never expire.

controls.name: iam.disableServiceAccountCreation
controls.what: Org policy that blocks creating new service accounts.
controls.setting: Google Cloud Organization Policy (constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountCreation or managed variant)
controls.quote: disable the creation of new service accounts

controls.name: Service account impersonation IAM (Service Account Token Creator)
controls.what: Only principals granted impersonation roles on the service account can mint tokens or sign JWTs as it.
controls.setting: Google Cloud IAM on the service account
controls.quote: Only authenticated principals with the appropriate permissions can impersonate service accounts.

controls_unknown: Whether Workspace Context-Aware Access or third-party app access settings apply to domain-wide delegation service account calls; the DWD page does not say.
Edition requirement for multi-party approval on DWD changes.
No per-DWD-client IP restriction found in Workspace docs; absence not stated by Google.
Default of 'Trust internal apps' not stated on the fetched page.
Exact UI path for applying CAA to Workspace APIs; the 2023 update links to help articles without naming the setting.

providers.name: HubSpot
providers.scope_notes: Private-app and newer developer-platform static authentication coexist. SSO requires eligible Professional/Enterprise subscriptions.

controls.name: App governance: Approve apps
controls.what: Marketplace apps must be approved by a Super Admin before non-admin users can install them; users submit requests.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps > select app > Approve
controls.quote: Non-admin users must request access to apps that haven’t been approved yet.

controls.name: App governance: Limit installation (Install Permissions)
controls.what: Restricts which users/teams may install an approved app (Admins, specific users/teams, or everyone).
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps > Manage access > Install Permissions
controls.quote: Limit installation : control which users and teams can install each app.

controls.name: App governance: Customize optional data permissions
controls.what: Turns optional scopes on or off for an approved app for all users; required scopes cannot be removed.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps > Approve / Manage access > data permissions
controls.quote: Customize optional data permissions : allow or restrict optional permissions for each approved app.

controls.name: App governance: Revoke approval
controls.what: Removes the app from approved apps and uninstalls it for every user.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps > Manage access > Revoke Approval
controls.quote: Revoking approval for an app will uninstall it for all users who have previously installed it.

controls.name: Uninstall an app for a specific user
controls.what: Uninstalls an approved app from one user's install; the user can reinstall unless approval is revoked.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps > Manage access > Installed by > Uninstall
controls.quote: The user can re-install the app in the future. If you want to restrict them from installing, you can revoke approval instead.

controls.name: User permission: App Marketplace access
controls.what: Only Super Admins and users with this permission (plus matching scope permissions) can install apps.
controls.setting: Settings > Users & Teams > user > permissions (Settings access)
controls.quote: Users with the *HubSpot Marketplace access* [permission]

controls.name: Deselect optional scopes at install
controls.what: The installing user can clear optional scopes before connecting the app.
controls.setting: Install consent screen (Connect app)
controls.quote: You can also clear any of the checkboxes under *Optional scopes* for any permissions that you don't want to grant to the app.

controls.name: User permission: Developer tools access
controls.what: Controls which non-Super Admin users can access developer features; creating service keys requires it.
controls.setting: Settings > Users & Teams > user > permissions (Settings access)
controls.quote: Developer tools access : toggle the Developer tools access switch on to let the user access and manage developer features

controls.name: Service key scopes
controls.what: Each key gets only the scopes selected, and only scopes the creating user already has; editable later.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Service Keys (or Development > Keys > Service Keys) > key > Edit
controls.quote: A key can only be granted scopes the creating user already has

controls.name: Service key Rotate / Delete
controls.what: Rotate creates a new key and expires the old one now or in 7 days; Delete removes the key.
controls.setting: Settings > Integrations > Service Keys > key > Rotate / Delete
controls.quote: If your key is compromised and you want to immediately revoke access, click **Rotate and expire now**.

controls.name: Legacy private app scopes
controls.what: Super Admin selects which scopes the private app token can use; editable after creation.
controls.setting: Development > Legacy apps > app > Scopes / Edit app
controls.quote: select the **checkbox** for each scope you want your private app to be able to access.

controls.name: Legacy private app token Rotate
controls.what: Issues a new token and expires the old one immediately or after 7 days; Super Admins get a reminder after 180 days without rotation.
controls.setting: Development > Legacy apps > app > Auth > Rotate
controls.quote: If your token is compromised and you want to immediately revoke access, click **Rotate and expire now**.

controls.name: Delete legacy private app
controls.what: Deleting the app permanently revokes its access token.
controls.setting: Development > Legacy apps > app > Auth > Delete
