controls.quote: When you delete one of your private apps, its access token will be permanently revoked and you'll no longer be able to use it to make API calls.

controls.name: Static auth token view/rotate restricted
controls.what: Only Super Admins or users with a developer seat on the account can view or rotate the static token.
controls.setting: Development > Projects > app > Distribution tab
controls.quote: To view or rotate your access token, you must be a super admin or have a developer seat for the associated account.

controls.name: Developer API key deactivate/regenerate
controls.what: The single per-account developer API key can be deactivated and replaced at any time.
controls.setting: Development > Keys > Developer API key
controls.quote: You can deactivate your API key and generate a new one at any time.

controls.name: Super Admin required for private apps
controls.what: Only Super Admins can access and create private apps, so withholding Super Admin removes the ability; there is no account-wide off switch.
controls.setting: User permissions: Super Admin

no_control.what: Required data permissions (scopes) of an app cannot be turned off by the admin.
no_control.quote: Required data permissions for apps cannot be modified or turned off.

controls_unknown: No IP allowlist for API calls found; "Allowed login IPs" (Settings > Security > Login) is documented only for logins.
Whether app governance (approval) covers privately distributed OAuth apps and static-auth apps, or only HubSpot Marketplace listings.
No admin-set token lifetime or mandatory rotation policy found for private app tokens, static tokens, service keys or the developer API key (only manual rotation and reminders).
No account-wide switch found to block service key creation other than withholding Developer tools access / Super Admin.

providers.name: Hugging Face
providers.scope_notes: Covers Hugging Face Hub (Team / Enterprise / Enterprise Plus). Hosted Hub; token management needs Team or Enterprise, org revoke and service accounts need Enterprise, IP ranges need Enterprise Plus. Inference Endpoints use the same user access tokens.

controls.name: Token Policy: Require administrator approval
controls.what: Fine-grained tokens need admin approval for org resources; read/write tokens are blocked.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Tokens Management > Token Policy

controls.name: Token Policy: Only access via fine-grained tokens
controls.what: Read/write tokens get 403 on org resources.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Tokens Management > Token Policy

controls.name: Deny token
controls.what: Removes approval-based org access immediately; reversible.
controls.setting: Token review page

controls.name: Revoke token (org)
controls.what: Permanently removes a member token's access to the org only.
controls.setting: Token detail page or POST /api/organizations/{name}/settings/tokens/{tokenId}/revoke

controls.name: Revoke leaked token everywhere
controls.what: Anyone can submit a raw token value; matching tokens are invalidated everywhere immediately.
controls.setting: POST /api/credentials/revoke

controls.name: Restrict organization access to your IP ranges only
controls.what: Org resources reachable only from listed CIDRs, including via tokens.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Network Security (or PATCH /api/organizations/{name}/settings/network-security)

controls.name: Bypass IP restrictions and the Content Access Policy
controls.what: Per-token exemption from IP ranges and content policy; admin-only.
controls.setting: Service account token form

controls.name: Service account token rotate / delete
controls.what: Rotate invalidates the old value immediately; delete revokes permanently.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Service Accounts

controls.name: Token Exchange token duration
controls.what: Admins set issued token duration (8 h default, max 30 days) and can refresh the client secret.
controls.setting: OAuth app settings

controls.name: Fine-grained token permissions
controls.what: Limit token to specific repos/orgs and actions.
controls.setting: Token creation form

controls.name: Service Accounts (org admin only)
controls.what: Only organization administrators can create service accounts and issue their tokens.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Service Accounts

controls.name: Token Exchange OAuth app set up by Hugging Face support
controls.what: Token Exchange only works through an org-bound OAuth app with the token-exchange privilege, which Hugging Face support sets up on request.
controls.setting: Contact Hugging Face support

controls.name: Write role required to manage trusted publishers
controls.what: Only users with the Write role on a repo can add or remove its trusted publishers.
controls.setting: Repo Settings > Trusted Publishers

controls.name: hf_oauth_expiration_minutes
controls.what: Sets OAuth token lifetime for a Space's Sign in with HF (default 480 min, max 43200 min).
controls.setting: Space README.md metadata

controls_unknown: Admin-enforced expiry for user access tokens or service account tokens (no setting found; PATs are valid until revoked).
Whether access tokens require or bypass an SSO session under Basic or Managed SSO.
Org-level allowlist or block for third-party OAuth apps.
Org-level control over who can configure Trusted Publishers on org repos.
Exact audit event name for OAuth Token Exchange issuance (docs say exchanges are logged).
Whether IP ranges apply to OAuth, Token Exchange and Trusted Publisher tokens.

providers.name: Jamf
providers.scope_notes: Covers Jamf (Jamf Pro, Jamf Platform API Gateway, Jamf Protect, Jamf School). Jamf Pro cloud (11.x) is the main focus; Jamf Log Stream export needs Jamf Cloud Premium; Protect and School covered from public docs only.

controls.name: Disable API Client
controls.what: Stops the client from issuing new access tokens; existing tokens stay valid until expiry.
controls.setting: Settings > System > API roles and clients > client > Disable API Client; or PUT /v1/api-integrations/{id} enabled=false

controls.name: Remove specified API integration
controls.what: Deletes the API client; already-issued tokens remain valid until expiry.
controls.setting: DELETE /v1/api-integrations/{id} or UI delete

controls.name: Rotate Client Secret
controls.what: Invalidates the old secret so it can no longer mint tokens.
controls.setting: API client > Rotate Client Secret; POST /v1/api-integrations/{id}/client-credentials

controls.name: API Roles
controls.what: Client privileges are the union of assigned API roles; editing a role's privileges applies to live tokens immediately.
controls.setting: Settings > System > API roles and clients > API Roles; /v1/api-roles

controls.name: Access Token Lifetime
controls.what: Sets token lifetime in seconds per client; changes do not affect tokens already issued.
controls.setting: API client > Access Token Lifetime (accessTokenLifetimeSeconds)

controls.name: Token scope parameter
controls.what: Caller may request a token limited to a subset of the client's roles.
controls.setting: scope parameter on POST /v1/oauth/token

controls.name: Invalidate current token
controls.what: Invalidates the bearer token presented in the request (self-revoke by the holder).
controls.setting: POST /v1/auth/invalidate-token

controls.name: Password Policy
controls.what: Sets lockout attempts, password length/age/reuse for local Jamf Pro accounts used to mint bearer tokens.
controls.setting: Settings > System > User accounts & groups > Password Policy

controls.name: Jamf Pro user account privileges
controls.what: Bearer token carries the account's privilege set; CRUD privileges map to POST/GET/PUT/DELETE.
controls.setting: Settings > System > User accounts & groups

controls.name: Integration scope level and capability permissions
controls.what: Each gateway integration is bound to one scope level (org, environment, tenant) and granted capability:action permissions.
controls.setting: Jamf Account > Integrations

controls.name: Integration validity (six months)
controls.what: Gateway integrations expire after six months.
controls.setting: Fixed

controls.name: Jamf Protect API client role
controls.what: Each Protect API client is assigned a role such as Read Only; max five clients.
controls.setting: Jamf Protect > Administrative > API Clients

controls.name: Jamf School API key methods
controls.what: Each key is limited to the API methods selected for it.
controls.setting: Organization > Settings > API > Add API Key

controls.name: Access Status (Jamf Pro user account)
controls.what: An admin can set a Jamf Pro user account's Access Status to Disabled, blocking that account's username/password sign-in used to get bearer tokens.
controls.setting: Settings > System > User accounts & groups > account > Access Status

no_control.what: Disabling or deleting an API client does not end access for tokens already issued; there is no documented per-client token revocation.
No SSO/IdP enforcement for API authentication.

controls_unknown: IP allowlisting for Jamf Pro API clients or user API access (none found in public docs).
Default and maximum Access Token Lifetime for API clients (the doc example shows expires_in 599, but no default is stated).
Whether Jamf Pro admins can block a user account from using /v1/auth/token while keeping UI access.
Which identity Change Management logs for actions taken by an API client, and whether /v1/oauth/token requests appear in the Access Log.
Exact Change Management object/action names for API client create/rotate/disable.
Jamf Protect API token lifetime and revocation; Jamf School API key expiry, auth header format and revocation behavior.
Platform API Gateway: revoke/disable controls for an integration and IP restrictions.

providers.name: JFrog
providers.scope_notes: Covers JFrog Platform (Cloud/SaaS). JFrog Cloud SaaS; IP allowlist, OIDC integration and MyJFrog API tokens need Enterprise X or Enterprise+, log streaming needs Enterprise+, Cloud Log Collection is on all SaaS licenses; several token thresholds are documented only as self-hosted YAML settings.

controls.name: Revoke Token by ID / Access Tokens page
controls.what: Admin revokes any token; users revoke their own.
controls.setting: Administration > User Management > Access Tokens; DELETE /access/api/v1/tokens/{tokenId}

controls.name: Revoke Token by Value
controls.what: Admin revokes a leaked JWT or reference token by its value.
controls.setting: POST /access/api/v1/tokens/revoke

controls.name: Token default expiry
controls.what: Sets the default expiry for new tokens.
controls.setting: PUT /access/api/v1/config/token/default_expiry

controls.name: token.max-expiry
controls.what: Caps non-admin token lifetime and blocks non-expiring tokens when set above 0.
controls.setting: access.config YAML token.max-expiry (default 0 = no limit)

controls.name: token.allow-refreshable
controls.what: Stops creation of refreshable tokens.
controls.setting: access.config YAML token.allow-refreshable=false

controls.name: Disable API Key Usage
controls.what: Blocks authentication with existing API keys.
controls.setting: Administration > Security > General > Disable API Key Usage

controls.name: IP/CIDR Allowlist
controls.what: Only listed IPs/JPDs can reach the JPD.
controls.setting: MyJFrog > Security > Allowlist; MyJFrog IP allowlist API

controls.name: Identity mapping claims
controls.what: Claims in each mapping restrict which workloads get tokens and with what scope.
controls.setting: OIDC integration identity mappings (UI) or Create/Update Identity Mapping API

controls.name: Delete OIDC Configuration
controls.what: Removes the provider so no new tokens can be exchanged.
controls.setting: DELETE OIDC Configuration API

controls.name: Regenerate MyJFrog API token
controls.what: Regenerating invalidates the previous token.
controls.setting: MyJFrog > profile > API Token > Regenerate Token

controls.name: Disable/delete user (with SCIM)
controls.what: Deleting or disabling a user revokes their identity tokens; SCIM pushes IdP deprovisioning.
controls.setting: User Management > Users; SCIM

controls.name: Allow Created Users Access To Profile Page
controls.what: When cleared, users auto-created through SAML cannot reach their profile page, where identity tokens and API keys are generated.
controls.setting: Administration > Authentication Providers > SAML SSO settings

no_control.what: Tokens with expiry shorter than the revocable threshold (default 6 hours) cannot be revoked.
Admins cannot monitor or manage individual users' API keys (only the global disable and a user list).
API keys have no expiry.

controls_unknown: Whether SaaS customers can change token.max-expiry, token.allow-refreshable or revocable-expiry-threshold (documented only as Access YAML settings).
A setting to stop non-admin users creating identity tokens.
Default and maximum lifetime of UI-generated identity tokens.
Whether the IP allowlist covers the MyJFrog portal API.
Whether MyJFrog audit logs record API token generation (event names not listed).
Reference token length: Access Tokens page says 128 characters, Identity Tokens page says 64.

providers.name: LangSmith
providers.scope_notes: Covers LangSmith (LangChain). SaaS (US/EU regions) plus self-hosted and BYOC; audit logs, SCIM and service-key roles are Enterprise, Viewer role needs Plus/Enterprise.

controls.name: pat_creation_disabled
controls.what: Stops anyone in the org creating new PATs.
controls.setting: PATCH /api/v1/orgs/current/info (API only)

controls.name: Global PAT creation disable (self-hosted)
controls.what: Env var disables PAT creation across all orgs on a self-hosted install.
controls.setting: Helm environment variable

controls.name: Organization Viewer role
controls.what: Users with this role cannot create PATs.
controls.setting: Org member role

controls.name: Deactivate PAT (revocation)
controls.what: Stops a PAT authenticating; reversible.
controls.setting: Settings > API Keys > Personal; POST /api/v1/orgs/current/personal-access-tokens/{pat_id}/revocation

controls.name: Delete PAT
controls.what: Permanently removes a PAT.
controls.setting: Settings > API Keys; DELETE /api/v1/orgs/current/personal-access-tokens/{pat_id}

controls.name: Delete service key
controls.what: Service keys can only be deleted.
controls.setting: Settings > API Keys > Service; DELETE /api/v1/orgs/current/service-keys/{api_key_id}

controls.name: Key expiration
controls.what: Per-key expiry in days; default never.
controls.setting: API key create dialog

controls.name: max_pat_expiry_days / max_service_key_expiry_days
controls.what: Org-level maximum expiry fields in the org API schema (behaviour not described in guides).
controls.setting: PATCH /api/v1/orgs/current/info

controls.name: Service key workspace scope and roles
controls.what: Limit keys to specific workspaces and (Enterprise) a workspace role.
controls.setting: Settings > API Keys > Service

controls.name: Remove user from org / SCIM deprovision
controls.what: PATs stop working once the user is removed from the organization.
controls.setting: Org members or IdP SCIM

controls.name: Delete SCIM token
controls.what: Deletes a SCIM bearer token.
controls.setting: DELETE /v1/platform/orgs/current/scim/tokens/{scim_token_id}

controls.name: Service key creation limited to admins
controls.what: Only admins can create service keys, so non-admin members cannot create them.
controls.setting: Organization roles (Settings > Members and roles)

controls.name: OrganizationAuthenticationManage permission
controls.what: Creating a SCIM token requires the OrganizationAuthenticationManage permission; users without it get 403.
controls.setting: POST /api/v1/platform/orgs/current/scim/tokens (role permission)

no_control.what: Service keys cannot be deactivated (only deleted).

controls_unknown: What ip_allowlist covers and whether it applies to API key requests
Whether SSO-only enforcement blocks PATs
Whether pat_creation_disabled affects existing PATs
Exact behaviour of max_pat_expiry_days / max_service_key_expiry_days
SCIM token expiry
Whether whoami-style reads (list workspaces, org info) are audited

providers.name: LiteLLM
providers.scope_notes: Covers LiteLLM Proxy (AI Gateway). Self-hosted open-source proxy (MIT) with an Enterprise license gating JWT auth, IP filtering, audit logs and key rotation; all controls are operator config on your own deployment.

controls.name: key/block
controls.what: Blocks a virtual key; /key/unblock re-enables it.
controls.setting: POST /key/block

controls.name: key/delete
controls.what: Deletes a virtual key; deletion is recorded in audit logs and the Deleted Keys view.
controls.setting: POST /key/delete; Admin UI Keys page

controls.name: key_generation_settings
controls.what: Limits which user or team roles may create personal or team keys, and can require params.
controls.setting: litellm_settings.key_generation_settings

controls.name: upperbound_key_generate_params
controls.what: Rejects key requests above a max duration, budget or rate limit.
controls.setting: litellm_settings.upperbound_key_generate_params

controls.name: custom_key_policy
controls.what: Custom Python hook that can deny any key create, update or regenerate (e.g. require expiry within 7 days).
controls.setting: general_settings.custom_key_policy

controls.name: allowed_routes
controls.what: Restricts which proxy routes a key can call, including admin-owned keys.
controls.setting: allowed_routes on /key/generate or /key/update

controls.name: team_member_permissions
controls.what: Controls which key-management routes team members may call; default is read-only key info.
controls.setting: team_member_permissions on the team

controls.name: allowed_ips
controls.what: Only listed client IPs can call proxy endpoints; others get 403.
controls.setting: general_settings.allowed_ips

controls.name: Key regenerate (rotation)
controls.what: Issues a new secret; old secret is revoked immediately unless a grace_period is set.
controls.setting: POST /key/{key}/regenerate

controls.name: Scheduled key rotation (auto_rotate)
controls.what: Background job regenerates keys on rotation_interval and invalidates the old string.
controls.setting: auto_rotate + rotation_interval on key; LITELLM_KEY_ROTATION_ENABLED=true

controls.name: disable_env_credential_login
controls.what: Stops the master key and UI_USERNAME/UI_PASSWORD from logging into the Admin UI; API use of the master key continues.
controls.setting: general_settings.disable_env_credential_login: true

controls.name: Master key rotation
controls.what: Replace the master key value and restart every proxy instance.
controls.setting: LITELLM_MASTER_KEY / general_settings.master_key; POST /key/regenerate with new_master_key when no salt key

controls.name: SCIM user deprovisioning
controls.what: Deprovisioning a user blocks all keys they own and clears them from the auth cache.
controls.setting: IdP SCIM push / DELETE /scim/v2/Users/{id}

controls.name: JWT audience/issuer validation
controls.what: JWT_AUDIENCE/JWT_ISSUER or litellm_jwtauth.issuers restrict which tokens are accepted; unset means any token from listed providers is accepted.
controls.setting: JWT_AUDIENCE, JWT_ISSUER, litellm_jwtauth.issuers

controls.name: store_audit_logs
controls.what: Records create/update/delete/regenerate of keys, teams, users, models.
controls.setting: litellm_settings.store_audit_logs

controls.name: enable_jwt_auth
controls.what: JWT tokens are only checked when this config setting is on; leaving it unset means JWT auth is not accepted.
controls.setting: general_settings.enable_jwt_auth in config.yaml

no_control.what: Failed-login rate limiting does not cover use of the master key as an API bearer token.
Disabling env-credential UI login does not stop the master key on the API.

controls_unknown: Whether /key/delete and /key/block take effect instantly or after an auth-cache TTL (only SCIM deprovisioning is documented as clearing the cache).
Master key expiry and SCIM token expiry, rotation and revocation steps.
Whether management GET calls (/key/info, /key/list, /spend/logs) are logged anywhere besides server logs.
Whether allowed_ips applies to /scim routes.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 / Entra / Graph
providers.scope_notes: Workload Conditional Access requires Workload ID Premium. Do not treat a token-issuance IP check as universal per-request Graph enforcement.

controls.name: User consent for applications
controls.what: Turns off or narrows user self-consent so delegated permission grants need an admin (or only low-impact permissions for verified publishers).
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > Consent and permissions > User consent settings; Graph authorizationPolicy.defaultUserRolePermissions.permissionGrantPoliciesAssigned
controls.quote: By default, all users are allowed to consent to applications for permissions that don't require administrator consent.

controls.name: Admin consent workflow
controls.what: Lets users request consent they cannot grant; designated reviewers approve or deny, and only Global Admins can approve Graph application permissions.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > Consent and permissions > Admin consent settings; Graph adminConsentRequestPolicy
controls.quote: only Global Administrators can approve admin consent requests for apps requesting for Microsoft Graph app roles (application permissions).

controls.name: Users can register applications
controls.what: Stops ordinary users from creating app registrations (and their client credentials); only Application Developer or admin roles can.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Users > User settings > Users can register applications
controls.quote: By default in Microsoft Entra ID, all users can register applications and manage all aspects of applications they create.

controls.name: Assignment required?
controls.what: Only users, groups or client service principals explicitly assigned to the resource app can get tokens for it; also blocks user consent for that app.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > [app] > Properties > Assignment required?; Graph servicePrincipal.appRoleAssignmentRequired
controls.quote: Users and services attempting to access the application or services need to be assigned to the application, or they won't be able to sign-in or obtain an access token.

controls.name: Enabled for users to sign-in?
controls.what: Disables the service principal in the tenant so no new tokens are issued for that application.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > [app] > Properties; Graph servicePrincipal.accountEnabled=false
controls.quote: To block user access to an application, you can disable user sign-in for the application, which prevents all tokens from being issued for that application.

controls.name: Revoke permission (admin consent / app role assignments)
controls.what: Removes granted delegated permissions (oauth2PermissionGrants) and application permissions (appRoleAssignments) from a service principal.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > [app] > Permissions > Admin consent > Revoke permission; Graph DELETE oAuth2PermissionGrants/{id} and appRoleAssignedTo/{id}
controls.quote: You can revoke permissions granted by admins for your entire organization, and you can get contextual PowerShell scripts to perform other actions.

controls.name: Application policies: Block password addition
controls.what: Blocks new client secrets and symmetric keys on apps and service principals, pushing app-only auth to certificates or federated credentials.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > Application policies; Graph policies/defaultAppManagementPolicy (passwordAddition, symmetricKeyAddition)
controls.quote: Block the addition of new passwords (also referred to as secrets) on applications altogether.

controls.name: Application policies: Restrict max password / certificate lifetime
controls.what: Caps the lifetime of new client secrets, symmetric keys and certificates added to apps and service principals.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > Application policies; Graph defaultAppManagementPolicy (passwordLifetime, symmetricKeyLifetime, asymmetricKeyLifetime)
controls.quote: asymmetricKeyLifetime | Enforce a max lifetime range for an asymmetric key (certificate). | Reduces security risk from long-lived credentials

controls.name: Application policies: Block custom passwords / trusted certificate authority
controls.what: Blocks client-supplied passwords, and (API only) blocks certificates not issued by a listed trusted CA.
controls.setting: Graph defaultAppManagementPolicy (customPasswordAddition, trustedCertificateAuthority); custom password also in Application policies UI
controls.quote: Block new certificate credentials if the issuer isn't listed in the trusted certificate authority list.

controls.name: Application policies: Block multitenant applications
controls.what: Blocks creating or promoting app registrations to multitenant or consumer-account audiences.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > Application policies; Graph appManagementPolicy audiences restriction
controls.quote: Restricts creation or promotion of apps based on signInAudience values.

controls.name: Conditional Access (users)
controls.what: Applies location, device, MFA, risk and block conditions when a user obtains delegated tokens for targeted resources.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies
controls.plan: Microsoft Entra ID P1 (risk conditions need P2)
controls.quote: Using this feature requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses.

controls.name: Continuous access evaluation / strict location enforcement
controls.what: Lets Exchange, SharePoint, Teams and Graph reject user tokens mid-lifetime on IP-location change or critical events like account disable.
controls.setting: Conditional Access > session control 'Customize continuous access evaluation'; strict location enforcement (preview)
controls.plan: Microsoft Entra ID P1 for location policies; critical events in any tenant
controls.quote: Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, and MS Graph can synchronize key Conditional Access policies for evaluation within the service itself.

controls.name: Conditional Access for workload identities
controls.what: Blocks token requests by selected single-tenant service principals from outside named IP ranges or when service principal risk is detected.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Conditional Access > Policies > Users or workload identities > Workload identities
controls.quote: Workload Identities Premium licenses are required to create or modify Conditional Access policies scoped to service principals.

controls.name: RBAC for Applications in Exchange Online
controls.what: Grants app-only mail/calendar/contacts permissions scoped to a management scope or admin unit of mailboxes instead of the whole tenant.
controls.setting: Exchange Online PowerShell: New-ServicePrincipal, New-ManagementRoleAssignment -CustomResourceScope / -RecipientAdministrativeUnitScope
controls.quote: This grant can be paired with a scope of access (resource scope) to specify which mailboxes an app can access.

controls.name: Sites.Selected and other *.Selected scopes
controls.what: An app consented to Selected scopes has no SharePoint/OneDrive access until an admin grants it a role on a specific site, list, item or file.
controls.setting: Consent Sites.Selected in Entra, then Graph POST /sites/{siteId}/permissions (and lists/items/files)
controls.quote: Selected scopes require an explicit assignment action; an application consented for Lists.SelectedOperations.Selected would initially have no access.

controls.name: Azure Policy deny on user-assigned managed identities
controls.what: Blocks creation of user-assigned managed identities in the scoped subscription or resource group.
controls.setting: Azure portal > Policy > Definitions (deny Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities) > Assign
controls.quote: You can keep your users from creating user-assigned managed identities using Azure Policy

no_control.what: Conditional Access (including workload identity CA) cannot target managed identities, and does not cover multitenant or Microsoft SaaS apps.
no_control.quote: Microsoft and third-party SaaS applications, including multitenant apps, are not covered by these policies. Managed identities aren't covered by policy.

no_control.what: Cannot force a managed identity token to refresh early; permission changes can take hours because tokens are cached about 24 hours.
no_control.quote: Today, it isn't possible to force a managed identity's token to be refreshed before its expiry.

no_control.what: App management policies do not stop existing non-compliant credentials from getting tokens; they only block create/update.
no_control.quote: Neither the tenant default nor the app management policies block token issuance for existing applications.

no_control.what: Workload identity CA is evaluated only at token request, not per Graph call.
no_control.quote: The policy applies only when a service principal requests a token.

controls_unknown: Licensing for app management policies (Application policies): fetched pages list only role prerequisites; Microsoft has previously tied them to Workload ID Premium, not confirmed here.
Whether 'Assignment required' is enforced for managed identities calling Microsoft Graph (doc covers client apps generally).
Exchange RBAC for Applications license requirement not stated on the fetched page; it does not constrain unscoped Entra grants, which must be removed.

providers.name: MongoDB Atlas
providers.scope_notes: Atlas cloud service; Admin API credentials (service accounts, legacy API keys) manage Atlas but cannot read cluster data, while database users read data; database auditing, access history and workload federation need dedicated (M10+) clusters.

controls.name: Require IP Access List for the Atlas Administration API
controls.what: Rejects Admin API requests from service accounts or API keys without a matching access list entry.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Require IP Access List for the Atlas Administration API; API field apiAccessListRequired

controls.name: API Access List (per service account / API key)
controls.what: Limits each credential to listed IPs or CIDRs.
controls.setting: Applications > Service Accounts/API Keys > Edit > Add Access List Entry; /orgs/{orgId}/serviceAccounts/{clientId}/accessList, /orgs/{orgId}/apiKeys/{apiUserId}/accessList

controls.name: maxServiceAccountSecretValidityInHours
controls.what: Caps how long new service account secrets can be valid (8 to 8760 hours).
controls.setting: PATCH /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/settings

controls.name: Client Secret Expiration
controls.what: Each secret expires after a chosen duration of 8 hours to 365 days.
controls.setting: Create Service Account > Client Secret Expiration

controls.name: Atlas roles
controls.what: Org and project roles limit which Admin API operations the credential can perform.
controls.setting: Applications > Service Accounts/API Keys > roles

controls.name: Delete service account / delete secret
controls.what: Removes the account (from all projects) or one secret.
controls.setting: Applications > Service Accounts > Delete; DELETE /orgs/{orgId}/serviceAccounts/{clientId}, DELETE /orgs/{orgId}/serviceAccounts/{clientId}/secrets/{secretId}

controls.name: Revoke Service Account Token
controls.what: Revokes a specific access token.
controls.setting: POST https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/revoke

controls.name: Delete API key
controls.what: Deletes the key and removes it from all projects.
controls.setting: Applications > API Keys > Delete; atlas organizations apiKeys delete

controls.name: Temporary User
controls.what: Database user is deleted automatically after 6 hours, 1 day or 1 week.
controls.setting: Database & Network Access > Add New Database User > Temporary User

controls.name: Restrict access to specific clusters
controls.what: Limits a database user to chosen clusters and federated database instances.
controls.setting: Database user > Restrict Access to Specific Clusters

controls.name: Project IP access list
controls.what: Only listed IPs can connect to clusters.
controls.setting: Database & Network Access > IP Access List

controls.name: Delete database user
controls.what: Removes the database user; also the only way to revoke an X.509 user.
controls.setting: Database & Network Access > Database Users > Delete

controls.name: Organization Owner role required to create service accounts and API keys
controls.what: Only Organization Owners can create org-level service accounts and API keys; project-level ones are created by project roles and are added to the org as Organization Member.
controls.setting: Atlas organization/project role assignment

controls.name: Roles required to add database users
controls.what: Only users with the listed Organization or Project roles can create database users of any authentication type.
controls.setting: Atlas organization/project role assignment

controls.name: Disconnect identity provider (Workload Identity Federation)
controls.what: Disconnecting the workload IdP from the organization removes Workload Identity Federation access for its users.
controls.setting: Federation management > Workload Identity Federation card > Manage > Disconnect

controls.name: Revoke JWKS
controls.what: Immediately drops JSON Web Key Sets cached on MongoDB nodes so tokens signed with a compromised key fail.
controls.setting: Federation management > Workload Identity Federation card > Manage > Revoke JWKS

no_control.what: Atlas-managed X.509 certificates cannot be revoked individually; only deleting the user removes access.

controls_unknown: Whether an org can block creation of legacy API keys entirely.
Whether API keys have any expiry setting.
Whether deleting a service account or secret invalidates already-issued 1-hour access tokens.
Whether deleting a database user terminates open connections.
Whether Admin API read (GET) calls are recorded anywhere; Activity Feed documents changes, not reads.
Default secret expiration value for service accounts.

providers.name: MuleSoft Anypoint
providers.scope_notes: Covers MuleSoft Anypoint Platform. Anypoint Platform control plane (US/EU/Gov); IP allowlist only US/EU commercial; audit export needs Anypoint Integration Advanced or Titanium.

controls.name: Disable connected apps for the organization
controls.what: Org admin can turn off the connected apps feature for the whole org.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps (exact setting not named in docs)

controls.name: Authorization policy: Restricted (application allowlist)
controls.what: Only allowlisted apps can be authorized by org members; scope additions need re-approval.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps > authorization policy

controls.name: Disable auto-approval of internal apps
controls.what: Under Restricted, internal apps must also be allowlisted.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps (Restricted policy)

controls.name: Revoke Authorization
controls.what: Removes an app's authorization and revokes its access and refresh tokens.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps > Authorizations > ... > Remove

controls.name: Scopes per business group and environment
controls.what: App permissions are limited to chosen scopes, business groups and environments.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps > Add Scopes

controls.name: Client secret expiration date
controls.what: Set an expiry on the connected app client secret.
controls.setting: Connected app settings

controls.name: Modify the Client Secret for a Connected App
controls.what: Admin replaces the client secret manually or via Access Management API.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps > app > Secret

controls.name: Delete Connected Application
controls.what: Deleting the app removes the client; effect on live tokens not documented.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps > Owned Apps

controls.name: IP Allowlist (Enforce IP restrictions for login)
controls.what: Blocks sign-ins with Anypoint credentials from outside allowed IPv4 CIDRs; users can be exempted.
controls.setting: Access Management > Security Settings > IP Allowlist
controls.plan: US and EU commercial clouds only

controls.name: Default session timeout
controls.what: Sets inactivity timeout that bounds bearer token validity (15-180 min).
controls.setting: Access Management > Business Groups > root org > Settings

controls.name: Revoke API contract
controls.what: Blocks a client application from calling the API instance.
controls.setting: API Manager > API instance > Contracts > Revoke

controls.name: Contract approval
controls.what: Instance owner approves access requests before credentials work against the API.
controls.setting: Exchange Request access / API Manager

controls.name: Reset environment client_secret
controls.what: Change environment secret via KB procedure or support.
controls.setting: Salesforce Help article / support

controls.name: IP Allowlist policy
controls.what: Gateway policy that only lets listed IPs or ranges call a managed API instance.
controls.setting: API Manager > API instance > Policies > IP Allowlist

controls.name: Revoke org connected app tokens
controls.what: Revokes all access and refresh tokens issued to a connected app.
controls.setting: DELETE /accounts/api/organizations/{organizationId}/connectedApplications/{clientId}/revoke

no_control.what: IP allowlist does not apply to users who authenticate through SSO, so SAML-derived bearer tokens are not IP-restricted by it.

controls_unknown: Whether IP allowlist applies to connected app token requests or API calls with an issued token
Whether deleting a client-credentials app or rotating its secret invalidates unexpired access tokens
Whether a client-credentials app's tokens can be revoked without deleting it (Revoke Authorization is documented for user authorizations)
Exact UI setting name for disabling connected apps org-wide
Whether read/GET API calls are audit logged
Environment client secret rotation procedure (help.salesforce.com KB 001115221 did not render)
Bearer token format/prefix
Whether IdP conditional access applies to connected app tokens (not stated)

providers.name: n8n
providers.scope_notes: Covers n8n (Cloud and self-hosted). Public API is on Cloud Starter/Pro/Enterprise and all self-hosted editions (not free trial); key scopes, log streaming and token exchange are Enterprise; env-var controls apply only to self-hosted.

controls.name: N8N_PUBLIC_API_DISABLED
controls.what: Turns off the public REST API for the whole instance.
controls.setting: Environment variable N8N_PUBLIC_API_DISABLED=true

controls.name: API key scopes
controls.what: Limits a key to chosen resource:action scopes.
controls.setting: Settings > n8n API > Create an API key > Scopes

controls.name: API key expiration
controls.what: Key creator sets an expiration time.
controls.setting: Settings > n8n API > Create an API key > Expiration

controls.name: Delete API key
controls.what: Deletes the key.
controls.setting: Settings > n8n API > Delete > Delete Forever

controls.name: Enable/Disable MCP access
controls.what: Turns the instance MCP server on or off; disabling disconnects every client.
controls.setting: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connection details

controls.name: N8N_DISABLED_MODULES=mcp
controls.what: Removes MCP endpoints entirely.
controls.setting: Environment variable

controls.name: Per-workflow MCP access
controls.what: Only workflows marked Available in MCP can be read in full, run or edited.
controls.setting: Workflow settings > Available in MCP; Settings > Instance-level MCP > Workflows enabled

controls.name: Rotate MCP access token
controls.what: Generating a new token revokes the old one.
controls.setting: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connect > API key tab

controls.name: Revoke access (connected clients)
controls.what: Disconnects an OAuth MCP client immediately.
controls.setting: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Connected clients > Revoke access

controls.name: Allowed callback URLs
controls.what: Restricts which redirect URLs can finish an MCP OAuth sign-in.
controls.setting: Settings > Instance-level MCP > Access > Allowed callback URLs

controls.name: allowedRoles (trusted key source)
controls.what: Restricts which roles token exchange may assign.
controls.setting: N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_TRUSTED_KEYS entry

controls.name: N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_MAX_TOKEN_TTL
controls.what: Caps issued token lifetime.
controls.setting: Environment variable

controls.name: Credential type policy
controls.what: Instance or project rules for which credential types are allowed.
controls.setting: PUT /credential-type-policies/instance

controls.name: Allowed HTTP Request Domains
controls.what: Limits which domains a credential can be sent to from the HTTP Request node.
controls.setting: Credential modal > Allowed HTTP Request Domains

controls.name: N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_ENABLED
controls.what: Token exchange is off unless this environment variable is true; the endpoint then returns 501. The preview flag N8N_ENV_FEAT_TOKEN_EXCHANGE must also be set to turn it on.
controls.setting: Environment variable N8N_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_ENABLED: leave unset or false to keep it off (Cloud: ask n8n support)

no_control.what: Scopes to limit a key are not available outside Enterprise; those keys have full account access.
No admin approval step for MCP OAuth clients; any signed-in user can approve one while MCP is on.
Removing a compromised signing key does not end already-issued tokens or sessions.
OAuth scope and resource in the exchange request are not enforced.

controls_unknown: Whether n8n API keys or MCP tokens are rejected when SSO is enforced or when a user is deleted
Any IP allowlist for API or MCP requests on n8n Cloud
Whether an admin can list or revoke other users' API keys or MCP API-key tokens
Whether 'no expiration' is an option for API keys, and default/maximum lifetime
MCP OAuth access/refresh token lifetimes
Whether public API read calls (GET /workflows, /executions, /credentials) produce any audit event
Audit log retention (log streaming forwards events; retention is in the customer destination)

providers.name: Notion
providers.scope_notes: Enterprise for IP restrictions; Business/Enterprise for SAML SSO. Confirm API enforcement and token-expiry requirements with Notion.

controls.name: PAT creation policy (who can create PATs with Notion API access)
controls.what: Limits PAT creation to owners, owners plus selected groups, or all members; removing a member's permission stops their existing PATs.
controls.setting: Settings > Connections (PAT creator settings)
controls.plan: Business or Enterprise (not configurable on Free/Plus)
controls.quote: If an admin changes the workspace policy so a member is no longer allowed to create PATs with Notion API access, that member's existing PATs stop working for Notion API requests.

controls.name: Revoke personal access tokens
controls.what: Workspace admins revoke any PAT; org owners can list/revoke via the Admin API.
controls.setting: Settings > Connections > All personal access tokens; Admin API
controls.quote: Workspace admins can revoke any PAT in their workspace from Settings → Connections → All personal access tokens.

controls.name: Limit which connections members can install
controls.what: Restricts members to no restriction, approved & recommended, or approved-only connections.
controls.setting: Settings > Connections > Manage tab
controls.quote: Approved only: Workspace members can only install connections pre-approved by a workspace owner.

controls.name: Approved connections list (revoke / disconnect)
controls.what: Owners revoke specific users' access to a connection or disconnect all users.
controls.setting: Settings > Connections > Manage tab > ••• menu
controls.quote: Click the ••• menu to: Filter by user. Revoke specific users' access to a connection. Disconnect all users. Remove the connection from the approved list.

controls.name: Manage page access (connection)
controls.what: Owners choose which pages a connection can access and whether only owners can connect/disconnect it from pages.
controls.setting: Settings > Connections > Manage tab > ••• > Manage page access
controls.quote: Workspace owners on the Enterprise Plan can decide what pages a connection can access, as well as who can connect or disconnect them from pages.

controls.name: Who can add integrations (organization security setting)
controls.what: Org owners enable or disable adding integrations for every workspace, or leave it workspace-managed.
controls.setting: Admin console (Manage organization) > Security
controls.quote: These settings can be Workspace managed so that they can be different for every workspace, Enabled for everyone in your organization, or Disabled for everyone in your organization.

controls.name: Admin bot token scopes
controls.what: Org owners pick which admin actions each admin token may perform.
controls.setting: Manage organization > General > Manage organization-level admin API tokens
controls.quote: Give the connection a name that your team will recognize, like “Compliance automation,” and pick only the access it needs.

controls.name: Rotate or delete admin token
controls.what: Owners rotate or delete admin tokens; scripts using a revoked token stop immediately.
controls.setting: Manage organization > General > admin API tokens
controls.quote: Rotate or delete a token at any time. Any script using a revoked token stops working right away.

controls.name: Admin APIs (organization owners only)
controls.what: Only organization owners on Enterprise can create admin connections and tokens; no other role can.
controls.setting: Manage organization → General → Manage organization-level admin API tokens

no_control.what: Admin tokens cannot be restricted to IP addresses or networks.
no_control.quote: You can't limit an admin token to specific IP addresses or networks.

no_control.what: PAT creation policy is not configurable on Free and Plus plans.
no_control.quote: | Plus | All workspace members. | Not configurable. |

controls_unknown: Whether Notion IP address restrictions apply to internal connection tokens, PATs or public OAuth tokens (help page only describes user sign-in; admin tokens are excluded).
Whether SAML SSO enforcement affects API tokens (not stated).
Whether admins can set a maximum PAT lifetime (creators choose 7 days to 1 year; default 1 year).
Whether internal connection tokens or OAuth tokens expire or can be force-rotated by admins.

providers.name: Okta (management API)
providers.scope_notes: Org authorization-server rules govern Okta APIs. Custom authorization-server lifetime policies do not govern these tokens.

controls.name: Token network restriction (API calls made with this token must originate from)
controls.what: Restricts where an SSWS token can be used from: any IP, or in/not in specific IP-based network zones.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Security > API > Tokens > Create token, or token > Security > Edit ('Token can be used from')
controls.quote: From the API calls made with this token must originate from dropdown list, select an option to specify where you allow connections to come from

controls.name: Admin role assignment (token inherits creator permissions)
controls.what: An SSWS token acts with the creating admin's current permissions, so limiting that admin's roles limits the token; only certain admin roles can create tokens.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Security > Administrators (roles of the creating user)
controls.quote: API tokens are generated with the permissions of the user that created the token. If a user's permissions change, then so do the token's. Super admins, org admins, group admins, group membership admins, and read-only admins may create tokens.

controls.name: Revoke token
controls.what: Admins can revoke any SSWS API token.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Security > API > Tokens > trash icon, or token page > Revoke token
controls.quote: On the API page Tokens tab, click the name of the token you want to revoke. On the token's page, click Revoke token .

controls.name: Deactivate token owner
controls.what: Deactivating the user who created a token makes Okta reject the token.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Directory > People > deactivate user
controls.quote: Tokens are valid only if the user who created them is active. Tokens issued by deactivated users are rejected.

controls.name: Token rate limits
controls.what: Caps the share of each API rate limit a single SSWS token can consume (default 50%).
controls.setting: Admin Console > Security > API > Tokens > token > Token rate limits > Edit
controls.quote: rate limits for token interactions are set automatically to 50 percent of each API maximum limit. See API rate limits . You can adjust this percentage for each token.

controls.name: Grant Okta API scopes
controls.what: A service app only gets Okta API scopes that a super admin has granted on its Okta API Scopes tab.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Applications > [service app] > Okta API Scopes > Grant; or /grants API
controls.quote: Only the Super Admin role has the permissions to grant scopes to an app. From the service app page, select the Okta API Scopes tab. Click Grant for each of the scopes that you want to add

controls.name: Assign admin roles to the service app
controls.what: Admin roles (and their resource sets) assigned to the service app constrain what its scoped tokens can do.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Applications > [service app] > Admin roles
controls.quote: For each service app you create, you need to assign admin roles to constrain the permissions and resources of that app for least privilege access.

controls.name: Public client app admins (org setting)
controls.what: When enabled, service apps automatically get the super admin role after scopes are granted; leaving it off forces explicit least-privilege role assignment.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Settings > Account > Public client app admins
controls.quote: If you want to bypass assigning admin roles to service apps, you can enable the Public client app admins org setting. This automatically assigns the super admin role

controls.name: Require Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP) header in token requests
controls.what: Makes the org authorization server issue DPoP-bound (sender-constrained) access tokens to the app.
controls.setting: App > General settings checkbox, or API settings.oauthClient.dpop_bound_access_tokens: true
controls.quote: An OAuth 2.0 client app that has the Require Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP) header in token requests checkbox enabled.

controls.name: Admin roles that can create API tokens (custom role needs Manage Users permission)
controls.what: Only super, org, group, group membership and read-only admins, or custom admin roles that include the Manage Users permission, can create SSWS tokens; other users cannot.
controls.setting: Admin role assignment / custom admin role permissions

controls.name: Super Admin-only grant of Okta API scopes
controls.what: A service app gets no Okta API scopes until a Super Admin grants them on the Okta API Scopes tab.
controls.setting: Applications > app > Okta API Scopes

controls.name: Network zone restrictions for clients
controls.what: Sets an allowlist or denylist network zone per client, enforced at the OIDC token endpoint.
controls.setting: Per-client network zone setting (GA in Production 2025.11.0)

no_control.what: Cannot change the 30-day idle expiry of SSWS tokens (no shorter or absolute lifetime).
no_control.quote: The 30-day period is fixed and can't be changed for your org.

no_control.what: Cannot use blocklist zones or non-IP zones to restrict SSWS tokens.
no_control.quote: You can only use IP-based zones with SSWS tokens. Ensure that you add them to the Gateway IP addresses field on the Add IP Zone page. See IP zones . You can't use blocklist zones with SSWS tokens.

no_control.what: Cannot change the access-token lifetime for Okta-scoped service app tokens.
no_control.quote: Note: The lifetime for this token is fixed at one hour.

controls_unknown: Whether any org-wide switch exists to disable SSWS token creation entirely (docs only show role-based limits on who can create tokens).
Whether network zones can restrict where OAuth service apps call Okta APIs from (org authorization server policies were not confirmed).
Default state of the Public client app admins setting.

providers.name: 1Password
providers.scope_notes: Covers 1Password Business. Covers 1Password.com Business/Enterprise developer and admin credentials; Connect server and SCIM bridge are customer-hosted; CLI user sign-in is a human login and excluded except as client for service accounts.

controls.name: Service Account permission (who can create service accounts)
controls.what: Only owners/admins can create service accounts unless they grant the permission to groups or people.
controls.setting: Developer > Permissions > Service Account > Manage groups / Manage People

controls.name: Service Account Access (per vault)
controls.what: Turning off service account access on a vault removes it from all existing service accounts and blocks new grants.
controls.setting: Vault > Manage > Service Account Access toggle

controls.name: Vault permissions at creation
controls.what: Vaults and read/write/share permissions are chosen at creation and cannot be changed later.
controls.setting: Service account wizard / op service-account create --vault; Connect New Token

controls.name: Revoke Token
controls.what: Revoking a service account token immediately removes its vault access.
controls.setting: Developer > Service accounts > [account] > Token > Revoke Token

controls.name: Rotate Token
controls.what: Issues a new token and expires the old one now, in 1 hour, or in 3 days.
controls.setting: Developer > Service accounts > [account] > Token > Rotate Token

controls.name: --expires-in
controls.what: Sets a lifetime for a service account at creation via CLI.
controls.setting: op service-account create --expires-in <duration>

controls.name: Secrets Automation managers / environment permissions
controls.what: Limits which groups can manage Connect servers and tokens, globally or per environment.
controls.setting: Developer > Permissions > Secrets Automation

controls.name: Connect token Expires After
controls.what: Token is revoked automatically after 30, 90 or 180 days.
