providers.name: Salesforce (core platform)
providers.scope_notes: API availability depends on edition. Creation of Connected Apps is restricted from Spring ’26; assess External Client Apps for new integrations.

controls.name: Permitted Users: Admin approved users are pre-authorized
controls.what: Only users whose profile or permission set is assigned to the connected app can use it; others are refused.
controls.setting: Setup > Connected Apps > Manage > Edit Policies > Permitted Users; Metadata ConnectedAppOauthPolicy isAdminApproved (ECA: permittedUsersPolicyType=AdminApprovedPreAuthorized)
controls.quote: If set to true , only users with the appropriate profile or permission set can access the app. These users don’t have to approve the app before they can access it.

controls.name: API Access Control (Allow only admin-approved apps)
controls.what: Org-wide: only connected apps installed or approved by an admin can call the Salesforce API; a separate switch covers customer/partner users.
controls.setting: Metadata ConnectedAppSettings enableAdminApprovedAppsOnly / enableAdminApprovedAppsOnlyForExternalUser; Setup > Connected Apps OAuth Usage (install/unblock)
controls.plan: Must be enabled by Salesforce Customer Support
controls.quote: If true , only apps that have been approved or installed by the admin can call the Salesforce API. To access this field, you must contact Salesforce Customer Support to enable API Access Control.

controls.name: IP Relaxation
controls.what: Enforce (default) applies org and profile IP restrictions to the app; Bypass options relax them, and Enforce_RelaxRefresh skips them for refresh-token exchanges.
controls.setting: Connected app / external client app OAuth policies > IP Relaxation; Metadata ipRelaxation (ECA ipRelaxationPolicyType)
controls.quote: ENFORCE (default)—Enforces the IP restrictions configured for the org, such as the IP ranges assigned to a user profile.

controls.name: Profile Login IP Ranges
controls.what: Restricts the IP ranges from which users of a profile, including API integration users, can log in.
controls.setting: Setup > Profiles > [profile] > Login IP Ranges; Metadata Profile.loginIpRanges
controls.quote: The list of IP address ranges from which users with a particular profile can log in.

controls.name: Enforce login IP ranges on every request
controls.what: Checks profile Login IP Ranges on every request, including from client apps, not only at login.
controls.setting: Setup > Session Settings; Metadata SecuritySettings/SessionSettings enforceIpRangesEveryRequest
controls.quote: If true , the IP addresses in Login IP Ranges are enforced when a user accesses Salesforce (on every page request), including access from a client app.

controls.name: Lock sessions to the IP address from which they originated
controls.what: Binds a session to the IP it was created from.
controls.setting: Setup > Session Settings; Metadata SessionSettings lockSessionsToIp
controls.quote: Indicates whether user sessions are locked to the IP address from which the user logged in ( true ) or not ( false ).

controls.name: Refresh Token Policy
controls.what: Sets refresh tokens to valid until revoked (default), immediately expire, expire after a fixed time, or expire after inactivity.
controls.setting: Connected app / ECA OAuth policies > Refresh Token Policy; Metadata refreshTokenPolicy (ECA refreshTokenPolicyType)
controls.quote: infinite —The refresh token is used indefinitely, unless revoked by the user or Salesforce admin. Default setting.

controls.name: Connected app session timeout
controls.what: Sets how long an access token session from the app lasts; falls back to profile then org session timeout.
controls.setting: Connected app policies > Session Policies > Timeout Value; Metadata ConnectedAppSessionPolicy sessionTimeout
controls.quote: If you don’t set a value, Salesforce uses the timeout value in the connected app user’s profile.

controls.name: High assurance session required (Block / Raise session level)
controls.what: Requires MFA-level sessions for the app; flows without a user approval step, such as JWT bearer, are blocked.
controls.setting: Connected app policies > Session Policies > High assurance session required; Metadata sessionLevel/policyAction
controls.quote: For flows without a user approval step, API logins with the High Assurance session security level are blocked.

controls.name: Enable Client Credentials Flow + Run As user
controls.what: Client credentials flow is off unless an admin enables it per app and names an API Only execution user whose access the tokens carry.
controls.setting: Connected app / ECA OAuth policies > Enable Client Credentials Flow, Run As; Metadata isClientCredentialEnabled + oauthClientCredentialUser
controls.quote: Salesforce returns access tokens on behalf of this user. This user must have the API Only permission.

controls.name: Block OAuth username-password and user-agent flows
controls.what: Org-wide switches that block the OAuth username-password flow and the user-agent flow.
controls.setting: Setup > OAuth and OpenID Connect Settings; Metadata OauthOidcSettings blockOAuthUnPwFlow / blockOAuthUsrAgtFlow
controls.quote: Indicates whether the username-password flow is blocked ( true ) or not blocked ( false ). The default value is false .

controls.name: Require PKCE for authorization code flows
controls.what: Requires PKCE on all supported variants of the authorization code flow into the org.
controls.setting: Setup > OAuth and OpenID Connect Settings; Metadata OauthOidcSettings isPkceRequired
controls.quote: This setting requires PKCE for all supported variations of the authorization code flow, including the web server flow, the Authorization Code and Credentials Flow, and their derivatives.

controls.name: Enable Token Exchange Flow
controls.what: Token exchange is off unless enabled on the connected app or external client app.
controls.setting: Connected app / ECA OAuth settings > Enable Token Exchange Flow; Metadata isTokenExchangeEnabled (ECA isTokenExchangeFlowEnabled)
controls.quote: If set to true , the connected app can use the OAuth 2.0 token exchange flow to exchange tokens from an external identity provider for Salesforce tokens.

controls.name: Require secret for token exchange
controls.what: Requires the app's consumer secret on token exchange requests.
controls.setting: Connected app / ECA OAuth settings; Metadata isSecretRequiredForTokenExchange
controls.quote: If set to true , the connected app must include its consumer secret ( client_secret ) in the token request during the OAuth 2.0 token exchange flow.

controls.name: Token exchange handler enablement
controls.what: The handler must be enabled and bound to specific apps with an execution user; it validates external tokens and maps users.
controls.setting: Setup > Token Exchange Handlers; Metadata OauthTokenExchangeHandler isEnabled + enablements
controls.quote: The enablement settings for the token exchange handler, including the execution user who runs the Apex class, the connected apps or external client apps for which it’s enabled

controls.name: Connected app creation restricted (Spring '26)
controls.what: New connected apps cannot be created without contacting Support; existing apps keep working and external client apps are recommended.
controls.setting: Platform default; contact Salesforce Support to re-enable
controls.quote: Connected apps creation is restricted as of Spring ‘26. You can use existing connected apps during and after Spring ‘26.

controls.name: External client app JWT access token timeout
controls.what: For ECAs issuing JWT-based access tokens, sets a custom expiry (1 minute to 12 hours) instead of the session timeout.
controls.setting: ECA OAuth policies; Metadata ExtlClntAppOauthConfigurablePolicies namedUserJwtSessionTimeoutType/namedUserJwtTimeout
controls.quote: the amount of time before a JWT-based access token issued to a named user expires. Values are in minutes.

controls.name: Consumer secret access via REST API
controls.what: Controls whether external client app consumer secrets can be read through the credentials REST API.
controls.setting: Metadata ExternalClientAppSettings enableClientSecretInRestApiAccess
controls.quote: Indicates whether OAuth consumer secrets can be accessed through the credentials REST API ( true ) or not ( false ).

controls.name: Block (Connected Apps OAuth Usage)
controls.what: Blocking a connected app ends all current sessions for it and prevents new ones until unblocked.
controls.setting: Setup > Connected Apps OAuth Usage > Block

controls_unknown: help.salesforce.com articles (connected app OAuth policies, JWT/SAML bearer flow pre-authorization, Use Any API Client, uninstalled connected app restrictions, OAuth token revocation) could not be fetched; controls are sourced from the Winter '27 Metadata API reference only.
Whether JWT bearer and SAML bearer flows always enforce IP restrictions regardless of IP Relaxation (stated in older packaging guides; not verified in current docs).
Behavior and timeline of the 'Use Any API Client' permission, which bypasses admin pre-approval; vendor deprecation page not fetched.
Whether a per-flow switch exists to disable JWT bearer or SAML bearer flows org-wide; none found in OauthOidcSettings.
Default of isSecretRequiredForTokenExchange and enableClientSecretInRestApiAccess.

providers.name: SAP BTP and S/4HANA Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Covers SAP Business Technology Platform (XSUAA, Cloud Management service, btp CLI), SAP Cloud Identity Services, and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Covers BTP Cloud Foundry/multi-environment subaccounts, Identity Authentication tenants, and S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition communication management; BTP docs cited from SAP's official SAP-docs GitHub source of help.sap.com.

controls.name: credential-types (xs-security.json)
controls.what: Restricts which secret types (binding-secret, x509) bindings and service keys of an XSUAA instance can use.
controls.setting: xs-security.json oauth2-configuration.credential-types

controls.name: Delete binding / service key
controls.what: Deleting the binding or service key makes XSUAA stop accepting its secret/certificate.
controls.setting: cf unbind-service / cf delete-service-key / cockpit

controls.name: token-validity / refresh-token-validity
controls.what: Sets access/refresh token lifetime per XSUAA instance.
controls.setting: xs-security.json oauth2-configuration

controls.name: Token Validity (subaccount security settings)
controls.what: Sets default token lifetimes for all instances in a subaccount that don't set their own.
controls.setting: BTP cockpit > Subaccount > Security > Settings > Token Validity; Security Settings API

controls.name: Token revoke endpoint
controls.what: Revokes an issued token, but apps validating offline keep accepting it until expiry.
controls.setting: Cloud Foundry UAA revoke endpoint

controls.name: hide-secret
controls.what: Omits the client secret from a binding or service key that only needs authorization data.
controls.setting: binding parameters {"credential-type":"binding-secret","hide-secret":"true"}

controls.name: btp delete security/api-credential
controls.what: Deletes XSUAA API credentials.
controls.setting: btp CLI

controls.name: Cloud Management service plan selection
controls.what: The cis plan (central, central-viewer, local, local-viewer) fixes the API scopes in the token.
controls.setting: Entitlements + cis instance plan

controls.name: Secret 'Expire in'
controls.what: Sets IAS client secret expiry to 1 year, 2 years or Never.
controls.setting: Admin console > Applications > Trust > Client Authentication > Secrets > Add; Administrators > System > Secrets

controls.name: Secret scope (Application / Application Users / OpenID)
controls.what: Limits which APIs an application secret may be used for; all scopes are selected by default.
controls.setting: Client Authentication > Secrets > Scope

controls.name: Administrator roles for systems
controls.what: Assigns only needed admin roles (e.g. Read Users) to a system administrator credential.
controls.setting: Admin console > Administrators > Add > System

controls.name: Client ID Lock
controls.what: Locks a technical user's client ID after 5 failed secret logons.
controls.setting: Users & Authorizations > Technical User > Details > Client ID

controls.name: Lock / delete communication user
controls.what: Locks or deletes a communication user in the Maintain Communication Users app.
controls.setting: Maintain Communication Users app

controls.name: Communication scenario / arrangement
controls.what: The arrangement's communication scenario defines which inbound services and auth methods the user can use.
controls.setting: Communication Arrangements app (SAP recommends one comm user per arrangement)

controls.name: Communication user password policy
controls.what: Requires 20+ character passwords with a special character and locks after 3 failed logons.
controls.setting: Built in (view in Display Static System Audit > Password Policy Technical User)

controls.name: Entitlements (SAP Cloud Management service plans)
controls.what: A cis service instance and key can only be created in a subaccount where the global account admin has entitled a Cloud Management service plan.
controls.setting: Global account > Entitlements

controls.name: Manage Applications / Manage Tenant Configuration administrator roles
controls.what: Only administrators with Manage Applications can configure applications (including client secrets), and only Manage Tenant Configuration can add systems as administrators.
controls.setting: Administration console > Administrators > authorizations

no_control.what: XSUAA does not check certificate revocation; a compromised X.509 binding cert stays valid until the binding is deleted.
Revoked access tokens keep working in apps that validate offline until they expire.
Legacy instance secrets cannot be rotated without recreating the instance.

controls_unknown: Any IP/network allowlist for XSUAA clients, btp API credentials, IAS API secrets or S/4HANA communication users.
Whether XSUAA password-grant tokens (cis service keys) honor IAS/corporate IdP MFA or conditional access.
Exact audit message for service key deletion and for API credential create/delete in XSUAA audit log.
Whether communication user passwords expire.
Org-wide switch to block creation of service keys or API credentials (none found).
IAS audit event emitted on client secret creation/deletion (change log covers admin CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE generally).

providers.name: ServiceNow
providers.scope_notes: Release/plugin dependent. API key/HMAC requires com.glide.tokenbased_auth and API-specific policy. Documentation reviewed is Brazil.

controls.name: REST API access policy
controls.what: Per REST API (or globally), lists the inbound authentication profiles allowed, so unlisted credential types such as Basic are refused.
controls.setting: All > System Web Services > REST API Access Policies (map Inbound Authentication Profiles)
controls.quote: Create an API access policy and map an authentication profile to restrict the authentication type for a REST API.

controls.name: API access policy with adaptive authentication filter criteria (IP)
controls.what: An access policy can combine an allowed auth type with filter criteria such as an IP range; other auth types or IPs are denied.
controls.setting: REST API Access Policies + Adaptive Authentication filter criteria
controls.quote: allows only OAuth 2.0 authentication type from a specified range of IP addresses

controls.name: Adaptive authentication policies
controls.what: Allows or denies authentication by IP address, role or group, including for inbound REST API requests.
controls.setting: All > Adaptive Authentication > Authentication Policies / Filter Criteria
controls.quote: You can use the filter criteria of adaptive authentication framework to restrict access to inbound ServiceNow REST APIs.

controls.name: IP Address Access Control
controls.what: Instance-wide allow/deny IP rules for inbound traffic regardless of credential type.
controls.setting: All > System Security > IP Address Access Control (plugin com.snc.ipauthenticator)
controls.quote: Deny: Any IP address in this range cannot interact with this instance unless it is listed in an Allow rule.

controls.name: Enforce Token Restrictions (OAuth application registry)
controls.what: Tokens from this OAuth client work only on APIs whose access policy allows its authentication profile; otherwise they reach any API the user's ACLs allow.
controls.setting: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > [client] > Enforce Token Restrictions
controls.quote: Select to only allow tokens to be used with APIs set to allow the authentication profile.

controls.name: REST API Auth Scope
controls.what: Once an API has an auth scope, only OAuth entities (or API keys) carrying that scope can call it; the useraccount scope bypasses this.
controls.setting: System Web Services > REST API Auth Scope; link scope to OAuth entity / REST API Key
controls.quote: you must associate the same Auth Scope to the OAuth Entity which should have access to this REST API.

controls.name: Access / Refresh Token Lifespan
controls.what: Sets per-client access token (default 1800 s) and refresh token (default 100 days) lifetimes.
controls.setting: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > [client] > Access Token Lifespan / Refresh Token Lifespan
controls.quote: By default, refresh tokens expire in 100 days (8640000 seconds).

controls.name: OAuth application registry Active
controls.what: Deactivating the registry entry stops the OAuth client.
controls.setting: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > [client] > Active
controls.quote: Select the check box to make the application registry active.

controls.name: glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled
controls.what: Inbound OAuth client credentials grant is only available after an admin creates this property and sets it to true.
controls.setting: sys_properties.list > New property glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled
controls.quote: Create the glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled system property

controls.name: OIDC provider for third-party ID tokens (Active, audience, user claim, JTI)
controls.what: Third-party ID tokens are accepted only via an active OIDC provider record that pins the audience, maps a user claim and can verify JTI.
controls.setting: All > System OAuth > Application Registry > New > Configure an OIDC provider to verify ID tokens (or Machine Identity Console > Inbound integrations)
controls.quote: This value should be the same as the value of the aud claim in the JWT token.

controls.name: Enforce Token Restrictions (OIDC provider)
controls.what: Third-party ID tokens work only on APIs whose access policy enables the ID token authentication profile.
controls.setting: OIDC provider record > Enforce Token Restrictions
controls.quote: Select this option to allow only tokens used with APIs set to enable the authentication profile.

controls.name: REST API Key: Expiry, Active, Auth Scope
controls.what: Each API key can be deactivated, given an expiry (empty means never) and limited by auth scope.
controls.setting: All > System Web Services > API Access Policies > REST API Key
controls.quote: Time after which the credential is no longer valid. Empty value means no expiration.

controls.name: API key / HMAC require a specific API access policy
controls.what: Token-based auth works only on APIs where an access policy lists the API key or HMAC profile; it cannot be added to the global policy.
controls.setting: REST API Access Policies > add API Key / HMAC authentication profile
controls.quote: Token Based Auth isn't allowed in the Global REST API Policy.

controls.name: REST API HMAC secret: Expiry, Active
controls.what: Each HMAC secret can be deactivated and given an expiry (empty means never).
controls.setting: All > System Web Services > API Access Policies > REST API HMAC secret
controls.quote: Time after which the credential is no longer valid. Empty value means no expiration.

controls.name: api_service_admin role (API key / HMAC configuration)
controls.what: Creating API keys and HMAC secrets requires the api_service_admin and adaptive_auth_policy_admin roles; users without them cannot create these credentials.
controls.setting: User roles

controls_unknown: Which authentication types the default Global REST API policy allows; the Brazil page names the Global Blocking Policy but does not list them.
No documented ServiceNow switch to disable Basic authentication instance-wide other than access policies; absence not stated by ServiceNow.
Whether adaptive authentication is active by default.
Default of Enforce Token Restrictions on OIDC provider records (OAuth registry default is unselected).
ServiceNow docs are SPA-rendered; quotes over ~125 characters were captured as exact fragments.

providers.name: Slack
providers.scope_notes: SAML SSO is available on Business+ and Enterprise, and on Free/Pro only with a connected Salesforce org. EMA uses organization-level installations and MCP user tokens.

controls.name: Require approved apps (Only allow pre-approved apps)
controls.what: Members can only install pre-approved apps; others must be requested and approved, and approval covers the scopes the app will use.
controls.setting: Admin > Apps and workflows > App Management Settings > Require approved apps
controls.quote: Apps connect third-party services to Slack, and by default, members can install them without approval from a Workspace Owner. If they'd like, Workspace Owners can enable app approval to pre-approve or restrict certain apps for their workspace.

controls.name: Restrict app
controls.what: Blocks members from installing or requesting a specific app; existing installs keep working until uninstalled.
controls.setting: Admin > Apps and workflows > Browse > [app] > Restrict
controls.quote: If an app you restrict has already been installed to your workspace, members can continue using it. You can uninstall any app you don't want people to use.

controls.name: App Management policy (Require App Approval)
controls.what: Turns on app approval for every workspace in the Enterprise org.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Settings > Organization Policies > Apps > App Management > Add Policy
controls.quote: Setting an app management policy turns on app approval for every workspace in an org. When app approval is enabled, members can only use apps that have been approved for their workspaces.

controls.name: Restrict for Organization
controls.what: Org Owners/Admins can block an app from being installed anywhere in the org when reviewing a request.
controls.setting: Org app request notification > Restrict for Organization; or admin.apps.restrict API
controls.quote: Select Approve for Organization or Restrict for Organization . Choosing Restrict for Organization will prevent all members from installing the app.

controls.name: Token rotation policy
controls.what: Requires OAuth token rotation for apps and expires unused refresh tokens after 30 days; applies only to installs and updates after it is turned on.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Settings > Organization Policies > Apps > Token rotation > Add Policy
controls.quote: Token rotation Require OAuth token rotation for apps and automatically expire unused refresh tokens after 30 days. Note: Changing these settings doesn't affect existing apps.

controls.name: Slack Marketplace installations policy
controls.what: Limits members to installing apps listed in the Slack Marketplace.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Settings > Organization Policies > Apps > Slack Marketplace installations
controls.quote: Slack Marketplace installations Only allow members to install apps from the Slack Marketplace .

controls.name: Member Permissions: who can use the app
controls.what: Limits which members (everyone, no one, or specific people/groups) can initiate interaction with an installed app.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Integrations > Installed apps > [app] > Member Permissions > Who has permission to initiate interaction with this app
controls.quote: Choose who can use the app — Everyone , No one , or Specific people and groups .

controls.name: Member Permissions: where can this app be used
controls.what: Limits an installed app to all channels, only specific channels, or all channels except some.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Integrations > Installed apps > [app] > Member Permissions > Where can this app be used
controls.quote: Next to Where can this app be used , click Edit . Choose where the app can appear — All channels , Only specific channels , or All channels except...

controls.name: Remove or uninstall an org-level app
controls.what: Org admins can remove an org-installed app from workspaces or uninstall it from the whole org.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Integrations > Installed apps; or admin.apps.uninstall API
controls.quote: There are two options for removing apps installed at the org level: Remove the app from workspaces that no longer need to use it. Uninstall the app from your org to remove it from all workspaces.

controls.name: Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA)
controls.what: Lets the IdP (Okta) provision and govern access to the Slack MCP server from Claude via ID-JAG; Org Owner enables it and sets the issuer URL.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Security > SSO settings > Enterprise-Managed Authorization > Edit
controls.quote: Next to Enterprise-Managed Authorization, click Edit . Click the toggle to enable Enterprise-Managed Authorization. Review your ID-JAG issuer URL (ex. https://acmeinc.okta.com ) and verify that it’s correct.

controls.name: MCP client app approval
controls.what: MCP clients must be backed by a registered Slack app, so the normal app approval process gates MCP access.
controls.setting: Same as app approval settings
controls.quote: MCP clients must be backed by a registered Slack app with a fixed app ID and hardcode that app ID. This allows Slack to: Let admins manage and approve your app/MCP client app using standard Slack app approval process.

controls.name: Restrict API Token Usage (Allowed IP Address Ranges)
controls.what: Rejects Web API, SCIM API and MCP server calls made with the app's tokens from IPs not on the list (max 20 IPv4 entries).
controls.setting: App settings > OAuth & Permissions > Restrict API Token Usage

no_control.what: The token rotation org policy does not apply to apps already installed before it is turned on.
no_control.quote: Changing these settings doesn't affect existing apps. The settings only apply to app installations and updates after you turn the setting on.

no_control.what: Unlisted (non-Marketplace, non-internal) apps cannot use the Slack MCP server at all; admins cannot allow them.
no_control.quote: Only apps published in the Slack Marketplace and internal apps can use MCP at this time; unlisted apps are prohibited from using MCP.

controls_unknown: No tenant-admin IP allowlist for app tokens found; 'Restrict API Token Usage' IP ranges are set by the app developer in app config, not by workspace admins.
Whether admins can force-revoke individual user tokens without uninstalling the app.
Whether EMA lets admins restrict MCP scopes beyond IdP assignment.

providers.name: Smartsheet
providers.scope_notes: API tokens need Business/Enterprise/AWM; SAML, token expiration and Directory Integration are Enterprise; Event Reporting is an Enterprise/AWM add-on; Gov and Regions use separate tokens.

controls.name: API Access Token expiration period
controls.what: Sets one expiration for all existing and future user and OAuth tokens in the plan; expired tokens are revoked.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Security & Control > API Access Token tile > Expiration period
controls.quote: Once a System Admin sets expiration times, all existing and future tokens within the plan adhere to this duration and are automatically revoked upon expiration.

controls.name: Revoke (delete) API access token
controls.what: User deletes their own token in the UI.
controls.setting: Account > Personal Settings > API Access > Manage API Access Tokens
controls.quote: You can also revoke (delete) API access tokens in the  API Access  >  Manage API Access Tokens  page.

controls.name: Revoke access token (DELETE /token)
controls.what: Revokes the token used to make the call; later calls with it fail.
controls.setting: DELETE /token
controls.quote: Revokes the access token used to make this request. The access token is no longer valid, and subsequent API calls made using the token fail.

controls.name: deleteAllForApiClient
controls.what: Revokes every token for the same app client ID and user.
controls.setting: DELETE /token?deleteAllForApiClient=true
controls.quote: A value of true deletes all tokens associated to the given client ID and user ID.

controls.name: Deactivate user
controls.what: Blocks the user and immediately revokes all API access tokens they generated.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Users and Groups > Seat Types and True-up > Deactivate; or POST /users/{userId}/deactivate
controls.quote: Deactivating a user immediately revokes all API access tokens they've generated. The deactivated user can no longer use them.

controls.name: Directory Integration (Okta / Entra ID SCIM)
controls.what: Removing or unassigning the user in the IdP deactivates them on next sync, which revokes their tokens.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Security & Controls > Directory Integration
controls.quote: When a user is removed from Okta or unassigned from the Smartsheet app, they're automatically deactivated in Smartsheet on the next sync.

controls.name: OAuth access scopes
controls.what: App gets only consented scopes, still bounded by the user's sharing permissions.
controls.setting: scope parameter on GET https://app.smartsheet.com/b/authorize
controls.quote: Access scopes don't override existing access-level restrictions (that is, sharing permissions).

controls.name: Admin Center API page
controls.what: Shows users with active tokens used in last 30 days and endpoint call counts; view-only.
controls.setting: Admin Center > API (Endpoints, API users tabs)
controls.quote: The API page in Admin Center gives System Admins a clear picture of API activity across their organization, such as who holds API tokens, what endpoints they're calling, and how often.

no_control.what: Per-user or per-role token expiration
no_control.quote: You can’t assign individualized or role-based expiration dates, as this is a general setting for all tokens under the specified plan.

no_control.what: Per-user or per-role token expiration
no_control.quote: You can’t assign individualized or role-based expiration dates, as this is a general setting for all tokens under the specified plan.

no_control.what: Revoking tokens from the Admin Center API page
no_control.quote: System Admins can review API data, but can't revoke tokens or manage API access directly through this interface.

no_control.what: Visibility of OAuth token usage on the Admin Center API page
no_control.quote: User-generated tokens only:  The data reflects tokens generated by individual users, not OAuth tokens.

controls_unknown: Whether SAML-only sign-in, domain-level SAML or domain strict blocks or re-checks existing or new personal tokens (docs are silent; only sign-in and sessions are described).
Any admin setting to stop users from creating API tokens.
Any admin path to revoke one specific token of another user without deactivating the user.
Whether password change, user removal (vs deactivation), or seat downgrade revokes tokens.
Whether deactivation revokes OAuth app tokens (doc says tokens 'they've generated').
IP allowlisting for API access.
Whether Safe Sharing, Enterprise Plan Manager, or User Auto-Provisioning affect tokens.
Admin control over which third-party OAuth apps users may authorize.
Refresh token lifetime.
Numeric API rate limits.
How Assume-User (impersonated) calls are attributed in Event Reporting.

providers.name: Snowflake
providers.scope_notes: Avoid treating default PAT safeguards as immutable. Verify client/driver and cloud support for federation.

controls.name: Authentication policy AUTHENTICATION_METHODS
controls.what: Allow-list of auth methods; omitting PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN, KEYPAIR, WORKLOAD_IDENTITY or OAUTH blocks that method for the account or user.
controls.setting: CREATE/ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY ... AUTHENTICATION_METHODS; ALTER ACCOUNT/USER SET AUTHENTICATION POLICY
controls.quote: PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN: Allows users to authenticate with a programmatic access token.

controls.name: Authentication policy SECURITY_INTEGRATIONS
controls.what: Limits which SAML/OIDC/External OAuth security integrations can be used.
controls.setting: CREATE/ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY ... SECURITY_INTEGRATIONS
controls.quote: A list of security integrations the authentication policy is associated with.

controls.name: PAT_POLICY MAX_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS / DEFAULT_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS
controls.what: Sets the default (15 days) and maximum (365 days) PAT lifetime; lowering the max breaks longer existing tokens.
controls.setting: Authentication policy PAT_POLICY
controls.quote: Specifies the maximum number of days that can be set for the expiration time for a programmatic access token.

controls.name: PAT network policy requirement (NETWORK_POLICY_EVALUATION)
controls.what: By default a user must be subject to a network policy to create or use PATs; admins can relax this.
controls.setting: Authentication policy PAT_POLICY NETWORK_POLICY_EVALUATION (ENFORCED_REQUIRED default)
controls.quote: the user must be subject to a network policy with one or more network rules to generate or use programmatic access tokens

controls.name: PAT role restriction requirement
controls.what: Service-user PATs must name a single role by default; admins can also require it for person users.
controls.setting: PAT_POLICY REQUIRE_ROLE_RESTRICTION_FOR_SERVICE_USERS / REQUIRE_ROLE_RESTRICTION_FOR_PERSON_USERS
controls.quote: you must specify the role that will be used during sessions authenticated with that token.

controls.name: MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS privilege
controls.what: Only roles with OWNERSHIP or this privilege on a user can manage that user's PATs, key pairs or workload identities.
controls.setting: GRANT MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS ON USER ... TO ROLE
controls.quote: you must use a role that has the OWNERSHIP or MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS privilege on that user.

controls.name: Disable / revoke PAT
controls.what: Admins can disable or remove a PAT; disabling a user's login disables their PATs.
controls.setting: ALTER USER ... MODIFY / REMOVE PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN
controls.quote: You cannot recover a programmatic access token after you revoke it.

controls.name: Network policies (account / user / security integration)
controls.what: Restrict inbound access by IP or private endpoint; integration-level policy overrides user and account policies.
controls.setting: CREATE NETWORK POLICY; ALTER ACCOUNT/USER/SECURITY INTEGRATION SET NETWORK_POLICY
controls.quote: the most specific network policy overrides more general network policies.

controls.name: Snowflake OAuth integration ENABLED
controls.what: Suspends a Snowflake OAuth integration.
controls.setting: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION ... SET ENABLED = FALSE
controls.quote: Specifies whether to initiate operation of the integration or suspend it.

controls.name: OAUTH_ISSUE_REFRESH_TOKENS / OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY
controls.what: Turns refresh tokens off or sets their validity (custom clients 1 to 90 days, default 90).
controls.setting: Security integration parameters

controls.name: OAUTH_SINGLE_USE_REFRESH_TOKENS_REQUIRED
controls.what: Requires refresh tokens to be single-use.
controls.setting: Security integration parameter
controls.quote: Specifies whether single-use refresh tokens should be used.

controls.name: OAUTH_ENFORCE_PKCE
controls.what: Requires PKCE for every authorization instead of only when the client sends it.
controls.setting: Security integration parameter
controls.quote: we highly recommend that your client require PKCE for all authorizations.

controls.name: External OAuth integration ENABLED
controls.what: Suspends an External OAuth integration.
controls.setting: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION ... SET ENABLED = FALSE
controls.quote: `FALSE` suspends the integration for maintenance. Any integration between Snowflake and a third-party service fails to work.

controls.name: EXTERNAL_OAUTH_ANY_ROLE_MODE
controls.what: When DISABLE (default), clients cannot switch to roles beyond those in the token.
controls.setting: Security integration parameter
controls.quote: `DISABLE` does not allow the OAuth client or user to switch roles.

controls.name: EXTERNAL_OAUTH_ISSUER / EXTERNAL_OAUTH_AUDIENCE_LIST
controls.what: Only tokens from the configured issuer and audience values are accepted.
controls.setting: Security integration parameters
controls.quote: Specifies additional values for the access token’s audience validation.

controls.name: Named key pairs (role restriction and expiration)
controls.what: Keys added with ADD KEY PAIR can carry a role restriction and expiry; legacy RSA_PUBLIC_KEY cannot.
controls.setting: ALTER USER ... ADD KEY PAIR / REMOVE KEY PAIR

authentication.summary: Access key ID (AKIA...) plus secret access key used to SigV4-sign AWS API and CLI requests. Up to two keys per IAM user.

federation.details: Keys belong to IAM users, not to an external IdP. AWS recommends federation with temporary credentials for humans and roles for workloads; no doc states whether IdP sign-in policy applies to these keys (it is not part of the signing flow).

ip_restriction.boundary: Not a setting: an identity policy or SCP that denies requests when aws:SourceIp is outside allowed ranges. lifetime.summary: Never expire; a time-bound deny policy (aws:CurrentTime) can cut them off

renewal.summary: Same key pair is reused until deactivated or deleted; rotation is manual (create second key, switch, deactivate, delete).

sso.details: AWS says IAM user access keys cannot be used with MFA-protected API access, and they are not issued through an IdP.

offboard.details: Access keys belong to the IAM user; deleting the IAM user deletes its keys. IAM users are not tied to IdP/SCIM deprovisioning.

inventory.details: The IAM credential report lists every user in the account with access key status.

authentication.summary: An SSH key pair whose public key is attached to a single repository; the private key stays on the server and authenticates Git operations over SSH. Keys are read-only by default, and write access can be granted when the key is added.

federation.details: Static SSH key registered on the repository; no external identity exchange is involved.

ip_restriction.boundary: An organization or enterprise IP allow list (GitHub Enterprise Cloud only) covers SSH keys, including deploy keys, for organization-owned repositories. IdP conditional access policy (CAP) IP conditions, used with OIDC for Enterprise Managed Users, do not apply to deploy keys because they do not act on behalf of a user.

lifetime.summary: No expiry; valid until deleted or disabled

renewal.summary: The same key is reused until a repository admin deletes it or deploy keys are disabled by policy; removing the user who added it does not deactivate it.

administration.summary: Added in repository settings by someone with access to them, or through the REST API (fine-grained tokens need repository Administration write). Organization owners can disable deploy key creation, and enterprise owners can set the policy for all organizations; disabling the setting also disables existing deploy keys. Additions and removals are logged as public_key.create and public_key.delete audit events.
administration.conditions: One key per repository; a key can't be reused across repositories. New organizations disallow deploy key creation by default. A write-enabled key can do what an organization member with admin access can do on that repository. A key created through the API with a personal access token or OAuth app token is deleted when that token is deleted or revoked; keys created with GitHub App tokens are not. Keys are not tied to organization membership.

sso.details: Deploy keys are repository-scoped, are not SSO-authorized, and IdP CAP IP conditions do not apply to them.

offboard.details: Deploy keys are tied to the repository; they stay active when the creating user is removed.

inventory.details: Only per repository via GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys or repo settings; deploy keys are not in the enterprise credential inventory types.

authentication.summary: OAuth 2.0 user bearer tokens; service-account signed JWT exchange. Domain-wide delegation (DWD) enables approved user impersonation.

federation.details: Google documents WIF → service account → IAM signJwt → OAuth token for DWD. Workspace scopes/admin delegation remain separate requirements.

renewal.summary: No refresh token; the app signs a new JWT (with a key, or keyless via IAM signJwt) and requests a new token. Key expiry depends on the org's key-expiry setting.

administration.summary: Approve/block third-party OAuth apps and scopes; restrict DWD scopes; control service-account IAM and key creation.
administration.conditions: Context-Aware Access requires eligible Workspace/Cloud Identity editions. User policy coverage does not establish protection of DWD service accounts.

sso.details: Context-Aware Access does not restrict Google API access from service accounts in general, but Drive policies do block automated tools from unauthorized IPs or devices.

offboard.details: A service account belongs to the application, not to an individual user.

inventory.details: Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Domain Wide Delegation lists every DWD client with its scopes.

sso.ui: Admin console > Security > Access and data control > Context-Aware Access > Assign access levels to apps > Drive (applies to automated tools; does not cover other Google APIs from service accounts)

expiry.api: POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token response field expires_in (3600)

token_format.notes: Service account key is a JSON key file; GitHub scans google_cloud_service_account_credentials. Access tokens are opaque bearer tokens.

authentication.summary: Static access token for a legacy (non-project) private app, sent as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. HubSpot implements it on top of OAuth, so client libraries accept it as an access token.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Trusted-IP documentation restricts account logins; API-call enforcement for private-app/OAuth tokens was not established.

lifetime.summary: Long-lived; explicit rotation/revocation

renewal.summary: Rotate the private-app token explicitly, immediately or with a 7-day transition.

administration.summary: Super admins manage legacy private apps: scope selection, viewing and rotating the token, 30-day API call logs, and deletion (which revokes the token). Super admins get rotation emails and a reminder after 180 days without rotation. Removing the user who created the app can make some calls fail until the token is rotated.
administration.conditions: UI creation of new legacy private apps is disabled on 2026-09-28 for accounts created on or after that date and on 2026-10-26 for older accounts; existing legacy private apps keep working. HubSpot points new in-account integrations to service keys (hubspot-5). Migrating a non-project legacy private app to platform 2026.09 is not currently supported. Up to 20 private apps per account.

offboard.details: Removing the user who created the private app makes some (not all) API calls with its token fail.

inventory.details: Super admins see private apps under Development > Legacy apps; GET /account-info/v3/api-usage/daily/private-apps reports usage for all private apps.

reads.ui: Development > Legacy apps > {private app} > Logs tab; Method = GET, search request URL '/crm/v3/objects/contacts'; Export logs (CSV) for 30 days

offboard.ui: Settings > Users & Teams > {user} > Actions > Deactivate user, then Actions > Remove from account

token_format.notes: Static bearer token, does not expire unless rotated. Prefix not shown in fetched private-app docs (service keys use pat-na1-). GitHub secret scanning covers 'Hubspot Private Apps User Token'.

log_sources.notes: Records user actions such as PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW and INSTALL_INTEGRATION with IP/location. UI shows 30 days; export covers last year. Scope account-info.security.read.

log_sources.name: HubSpot centralized audit log (/account-info/v3/activity/audit-logs)
log_sources.notes: Enterprise only. User actions incl. CRITICAL_ACTION subcategories. Records HubSpot-user actions, not API calls.

log_sources.name: Private app Logs tab (API call logs)
log_sources.notes: Per-app API calls for 30 days; filter by method/response/URL; CSV export. No request body, URL params or response payload for successful calls.

credential_id_fields.notes: Private app ID on PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW (also in infoUrl /private-apps/{hubId}/{appId}/auth)
Private app ID on CRITICAL_ACTION / PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW
Maps a found token to its private app, plus userId (creator), hubId, scopes

lifecycle_events.notes: A user revealed the token in the UI (security activity type / audit subCategory). Possible exfil point.

anomaly_cues: PRIVATE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN_VIEW by a user who does not own the integration, or from a new country/IP
Token view followed within hours by API calls in the Logs tab from new patterns (new endpoints, export-heavy reads)
Private app whose creator was removed (calls failing with USER_DOES_NOT_HAVE_PERMISSIONS) yet still active
Token not rotated in 180+ days (HubSpot reminder emails)
Scopes broadened on a private app with no change ticket

containment.steps: Private app > Auth > Rotate > 'Rotate and expire now'; or delete the private app (token permanently revoked). Then update the integration with the new token.
containment.notes: 'Rotate and expire later' leaves the old token valid for 7 days; use expire now for incidents.

authentication.summary: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow for project-based apps (and existing legacy public apps) installed in multiple accounts. The app exchanges the code for a 30-minute access token, sent as a Bearer token, and a refresh token.

federation.details: General CRM API federation is not established. Client credentials documented for selected developer-platform functions is not a general CRM grant.

ip_restriction.boundary: Trusted-IP documentation restricts account logins; API-call enforcement for private-app/OAuth tokens was not established.

lifetime.summary: 30 minutes

renewal.summary: Use the refresh token to get a new 30-minute access token. HubSpot describes refresh tokens as not expiring for now; they stop working when the app is uninstalled or the token is revoked.

administration.summary: Scopes (required, conditionally required, optional) are declared in app-hsmeta.json; installers must be super admins or have HubSpot Marketplace access plus the matching permissions. The client secret can be rotated from the app's Auth tab. Apps on 2026.09 can opt into user-level access (isUserLevel), which limits API access to the installing user's permissions; by default access is account-wide.
administration.conditions: Privately distributed OAuth apps install in up to 10 allowlisted accounts; marketplace apps up to 25 before listing. Creation of legacy public apps ended on 2026-06-23; existing ones keep working. User-level access requires OAuth and a new app (account-level apps cannot be converted).

inventory.details: Settings > Integrations > Connected Apps lists connected and approved apps, not individual tokens.

expiry.api: Read expires_in from POST /oauth/v1/token response, or GET /oauth/v1/access-tokens/{token} (returns expires_in)

reads.ui: (App developer account) Development > Legacy apps > {app} > Monitoring > API calls tab; filter method GET and request URL

token_format.notes: Access token opaque, 30-minute lifetime (expires_in 1800). Refresh token example format 'na1-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee' (region prefix like na1-). Client id/secret are GUID-style.

Refresh token use continuing after the installing user was deactivated

authentication.summary: Bearer access token for a project-based app configured with auth type static and private distribution in app-hsmeta.json. The token appears on the app's Distribution tab after install.

renewal.summary: The token is reused for API calls and rotated from the Distribution tab; whether the old token is invalidated immediately is not documented.

administration.summary: Scopes are declared in app-hsmeta.json; scope changes require reinstalling. Only super admins or users with a developer seat on the account can view or rotate the token.

Distinct from legacy private app tokens (hubspot-1), whose UI creation HubSpot disables in Sept/Oct 2026, and from account service keys (hubspot-5), which are not tied to an app.

inventory.details: Apps are listed on the Development > Projects page; the token is shown per app on its Distribution tab, with no org-wide token list.

token_format.notes: Static bearer token for a project app with static auth and private distribution; shown on the app's Distribution tab after install. Format not documented in fetched docs.

authentication.summary: Account-level API key created in Development > Keys > Service keys (also shown under Settings > Integrations > Service Keys), with selected object scopes. It is sent as a Bearer token and only authenticates REST API requests, not webhooks, UI extensions or other app features.

federation.details: Static account key created in the HubSpot UI; no external identity exchange is documented for service keys.

ip_restriction.boundary: HubSpot's trusted-IP and allowed-location settings limit account logins (Starter, Professional or Enterprise; Super Admin). The service key docs and launch posts do not mention any source-IP control for API calls made with a service key.

lifetime.summary: No expiry documented; rotation or deletion ends access

renewal.summary: The key is reused until rotated or deleted; rotation can expire the old key immediately or after a 7-day overlap, which can be ended early or cancelled (cancelling revokes the new key).

administration.summary: Super admins and users with the Developer tools access permission can create, edit (name and scopes), rotate and delete service keys and view their request logs. Keys use the developer-platform scope list, are not tied to an individual user, and key values are visible only to admins by default.
administration.conditions: Announced as the replacement for UI-created legacy private apps for in-account integrations; legacy private app creation is disabled on 2026-09-28 (new accounts) and 2026-10-26 (existing accounts). Subject to the same rate limits as privately distributed apps (tiers listed from Free to Enterprise); no separate plan requirement is documented. Separate from project-app static auth tokens (hubspot-3).

offboard.details: Service keys are account-level and keep working after the creator leaves.

authentication.summary: The client POSTs a token from an external identity provider (access, refresh or ID token, SAML assertion or JWT) to the Salesforce token endpoint. An Apex token exchange handler validates it and maps it to a Salesforce user, and Salesforce returns its own access token.

federation.details: This path exists to exchange an external IdP token for Salesforce tokens. Trust is defined in customer-written Apex: the handler decides what counts as a valid token and which user it maps to, and it can create users.

ip_restriction.boundary: General Salesforce controls apply to OAuth apps: profile login IP ranges, the app's IP relaxation policy, and optional 'Enforce login IP ranges on every request'. The IP relaxation and continuous-enforcement pages do not name the token exchange flow, so how its initial exchange is treated was not established.

lifetime.summary: Salesforce access token follows session timeout (inactivity); default 2 h

renewal.summary: If the app requests one, Salesforce returns a refresh token governed by the app's refresh token policy (valid until revoked, immediate, idle or fixed expiry); otherwise the client exchanges a fresh external token.

administration.summary: Admins create a token exchange handler (Apex class plus OauthTokenExchangeHandler metadata), enable it for specific connected apps or external client apps, and pick a Run As execution user. ip_restriction.boundary: Account/user network policies. By default PERSON and SERVICE users need a network policy to use a PAT; SERVICE_AGENT users do not. Authentication policy NETWORK_POLICY_EVALUATION can drop the requirement or skip enforcement.

renewal.summary: No refresh; rotate the PAT (new secret, extended expiry) or generate a new one. Lowering the policy maximum makes existing longer-lived PATs fail.

offboard.details: Disabling a user, which is what Okta SCIM deactivation does, automatically disables the user's PATs and aborts the user's running queries.

authentication.summary: OAuth 2.0 with Snowflake as the authorization server. A partner or custom client sends the user through Snowflake sign-in and consent, then presents the short-lived Snowflake access token; refresh tokens are optional.

federation.details: Snowflake issues the tokens itself; no external token is exchanged. Tokens from an external authorization server use External OAuth (snowflake-5), and cloud workload identities use workload identity federation (snowflake-4).

ip_restriction.boundary: A network policy on the Snowflake OAuth integration covers code exchange, refresh token use and access token use, and overrides user and account policies. User-level policies are not checked on token requests (except the built-in local-application integration).

lifetime.summary: Default 10 min; configurable 1 min–1 h per integration

renewal.summary: Refresh tokens (on by default) default to 90 days (7776000 s); custom clients allow 1–90 days and partner apps 1 h–90 days, then the user must re-authorize. Single-use refresh tokens are optional.

administration.summary: Roles with CREATE INTEGRATION (ACCOUNTADMIN by default) create the integration. ACCOUNTADMIN, ORGADMIN, GLOBALORGADMIN and SECURITYADMIN are blocked by default; BLOCKED_ROLES_LIST, refresh-token settings and an integration network policy are set per integration.
administration.conditions: Avoid treating default PAT safeguards as immutable. Verify client/driver and cloud support for federation.

offboard.details: OAuth sessions run as a Snowflake user. Disabling that user, which SCIM deactivation does, aborts the user's queries and blocks new logins.

authentication.summary: An external authorization server (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, PingFederate or a custom server) issues the access token, and the client presents it to Snowflake. Snowflake validates it against the External OAuth security integration (issuer, keys, audience) and maps a token claim to a Snowflake user.

federation.details: Snowflake accepts tokens issued by the customer's own OAuth server. Trust is set per integration by issuer, signing keys (JWKS URL or RSA public key) and audience.

ip_restriction.boundary: Network policy on the External OAuth integration overrides user and account policies; logged-in sessions from blocked origins cannot run further queries. Older Entra ID and Okta setup pages still say integration-level policies are not supported and to use account-level policies, so verify in the tenant.

lifetime.summary: Set by the external authorization server; Snowflake rejects tokens past exp

renewal.summary: The client gets a new access token from the external authorization server (for example with that server's refresh token or client credentials); Snowflake issues no refresh token for this path.

administration.summary: Roles with CREATE INTEGRATION (ACCOUNTADMIN by default) create the integration. Privileged roles are blocked by default; role switching is off by default (EXTERNAL_OAUTH_ANY_ROLE_MODE). Authentication policies can allow or disallow External OAuth (OAUTH) and limit which integrations apply.
administration.conditions: Token lifetime, refresh and client grant types are controlled in the external IdP, not Snowflake. Some setup pages conflict with the network-policy page on integration-level policies.

sso.details: Tokens come from the customer's authorization server, so its MFA, subnet and approval policies apply when the token is issued.

offboard.details: The token maps to a Snowflake user. Disabling that user, which SCIM deactivation does, blocks logins and aborts the user's queries. Disabling the user in the IdP also stops new tokens.

disable.cli: SQL: ALTER SECURITY INTEGRATION <name> SET ENABLED = FALSE; or AUTHENTICATION_METHODS without 'OAUTH' + ALTER ACCOUNT|USER <name> SET AUTHENTICATION POLICY <policy>

On uninstall the user chooses whether to keep or expire them. Agent-tagged restricted keys are subject to approval rules. Dashboard SSO/session controls are separate from key access policies.

authentication.summary: A Stripe App set to OAuth sends the user to an install link; the app backend exchanges the one-time code (valid 5 minutes) at /v1/oauth/token using the developer's own secret key and gets a 1-hour access token, which it sends like an API key. Connect OAuth's returned access_token and refresh_token are deprecated; Connect platforms should use their platform key with the Stripe-Account header (stripe-1).

federation.details: Tokens come from user authorization at app install and are refreshed with the developer's secret key. No exchange of an external identity token is documented for this path. Stripe Workload Identity Federation (private preview) is a separate mechanism.

The token exchange requires the app developer's secret key. For Connect OAuth, the access_token, refresh_token and stripe_publishable_key response fields are deprecated, and since June 2021 read_write OAuth can't connect accounts controlled by another platform.

authentication.summary: A workload on AWS or Google Cloud gets an identity token from its cloud provider and exchanges it, using the service principal's client ID (oacli_...), for a short-lived Stripe access token used to call the API. During the preview, the Ruby and TypeScript SDKs handle the exchange; requests name the target account with Stripe-Context.

federation.details: Trust is set on an organization-level service principal by the provider's issuer URL and the workload's subject: the IAM role ARN on AWS (outbound identity federation, audience https://access.stripe.com/wif) or the service account's numeric unique ID on Google Cloud.

ip_restriction.boundary: Stripe says access policies can be applied to service principals, but the WIF page does not describe how they are enforced on exchanged tokens. Without a policy, tokens can be used from anywhere; only a trusted workload can obtain them.

lifetime.summary: 1 hour

renewal.summary: No refresh token is documented; the SDK exchanges a fresh cloud identity token for a new access token, so continued access depends on the workload keeping its cloud identity and on the service principal's trust settings.

administration.summary: Service principals are created in the organization Dashboard (Organization > Developers > API authentication > Service principals) with a trusted identity provider, one or more subjects, and permissions assigned like an API key. Stripe says activity can be monitored per service principal and controls such as access policies and approval rules can be applied.
administration.conditions: Private preview; requires a Stripe organization. Only the Ruby and TypeScript SDKs (preview builds) are supported, and service principals support only WIF as an authentication method during the preview. Which roles can create service principals, and how to revoke or disable one, were not found.

offboard.details: A service principal is a non-human identity.
